# The Rule Index

Every rule in this repository, stated once, in one table. Each row cites the
document it came from; that document stays the source of truth.

283 rules · 18 groups · 56 sources · filterable version: [rules.html](https://vbarbarosh.github.io/rules/docs/rules.html)

How a screen moves has a page of its own: [animations.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/docs/animations.md).

Codes match [rules.html](https://vbarbarosh.github.io/rules/docs/rules.html), which is built from this file, and
`LINT` is a group of its own. A new rule takes the next code in its group.
Existing codes stay stable when a rule moves to another group; a group of
its own gets its own codes, and the old ones still open the rule: UI-09 to
UI-20 are UIM-01 to UIM-12 since 2026-10-08.
A retired code is never given to another rule: FMT-06, FILE-22 and LINT-05
are retired.
In the canonical forms, `✓` and `✗` are verdicts, not code.

| **CORE** | **Uniformity** — The rule behind the rules. | | |
| CORE-01 | **Explicit rules take priority for new code.** Follow the surrounding code only where no explicit rule applies. A new rule does not require rewriting existing code; that refactoring can happen separately. | An explicit rule requires `error`: use `function (error)` in new code even beside older `function (err)` handlers. ![A written rule beside older code: the old handler keeps function (err), the new one is written function (error); rewriting the old is separate work](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/explicit_rules_first.svg) | [docs/README.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/docs/README.md) |
| CORE-02 | **Unwritten conventions bind too.** An unwritten convention is still a convention. File names, CSS classes, formatting and even attribute order follow the same systematic approach, even where it is not written down. | ![No rule names it, yet every file in components/ is kebab-case: user-menu.vue follows them, UserMenu.vue does not; the same for classes, formatting and attribute order](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/unwritten_conventions.svg) | [docs/README.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/docs/README.md) |
| CORE-03 | **An option is "value" and "label".** A selectable option is always `{value, label}` — value is internal, label is displayed. Select, dropdown, radio, tabs alike. | `{value: <internal>, label: <display>}` ![One list of {value, label} options shown as a select, radio buttons and tabs; the user reads Netherlands, the code sends country=nl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/value_label.svg) | [value_label.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/value_label.md) |
| CORE-04 | **Opposites come from the established pairs.** `req/res` is Express-only; `res/rej` is valid for Promise executors, as are the full names `resolve/reject`. | <pre>construct/destruct  create/destroy<br>open/close          begin/end<br>start/finish        first/last<br>next/previous       get/put<br>src/dest            source/destination<br>res/rej (Promise)   resolve/reject<br>req/res (Express)   request/response<br>setup/teardown      push/pull<br>enabled/disabled    import/export</pre> ![Made-up pairs and the established ones they should be: begin/finish to begin/end, create/remove to create/destroy, open/shut to open/close; and the narrow pairs with where each holds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/established_pairs.svg) | [docs/README.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/docs/README.md) |
| **NAME** | **Naming grammar** — Verb morphology decides function or data. | | |
| NAME-01 | **Functions are verbs; data are nouns.** Functions are verb phrases, data are noun phrases. Each assignment reads as a sentence — the verb performs, the noun holds. | `const users_by_role = users_group_by_role(users);` ![users flows into users_group_by_role(), a verb, which makes users_by_role, a noun; the line read as a sentence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/verbs_and_nouns.svg) | [docs/README.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/docs/README.md) |
| NAME-02 | **The verb form marks function or data.** English verb morphology is the marker. An imperative verb makes a function; a past participle makes data. Where there is no verb, a function marker — `_from_`, `_to_`, `_of_`, `check_` — makes a function. One exception: a linter rule's function is named after its rule id, as ESLint does, `block_layout(context)` for `block-layout`. | <pre>items_sort_by_time(items)   // function<br>items_sorted_by_time        // data</pre> ![items_sort_by_time(items), an imperative, is a function; items_sorted_by_time, a past participle, is data; with no verb, _from_, _to_, _of_ or check_ makes a function](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/verb_form.svg) | [naming_markers.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/naming_markers.md) |
| NAME-03 | **A bare "by" name is data, never called.** A bare `_by_` name is always data, never a function: it is read with brackets, or with `.get()` when it is a `Map` — never called. | <pre>user_by_id&#91;id]       ✓ right<br>user_by_id.get(id)   ✓ right, a Map<br>user_by_id(id)       ✗ wrong</pre> ![user_by_id as a table of ids and users: read with brackets or .get(), never called](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/bare_by_is_data.svg) | [docs/README.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/docs/README.md) |
| NAME-04 | **The first word's plural states what a key returns.** Plurality of the first word states lookup cardinality — what one key returns, not how big the container is. | <pre>user_by_id&#91;id]                    // User<br>users_by_role&#91;role]               // User&#91;]<br>children_by_parent_id&#91;parent_id]  // Node&#91;]</pre> ![user_by_id returns one User per key; users_by_role and children_by_parent_id return a list per key](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/plural_states_cardinality.svg) | [var_names.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/var_names.md) |
| NAME-05 | **"Sorted by" is the same data, reordered.** `_sorted_by_` marks data of the same shape, reordered. The participle survives here because it carries what shape alone cannot. | `items_sorted_by_time   // Item[], still an array` ![four items by time, and the same four reordered as items_sorted_by_time, still an array](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/sorted_by_same_data.svg) | [naming_markers.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/naming_markers.md) |
| NAME-06 | **`_per_` marks a ratio or a rate.** | `clicks_per_visit` ![1 240 clicks over 400 visits make clicks_per_visit, 3.1: a rate, not a list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/per_is_a_rate.svg) | [naming_markers.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/naming_markers.md) |
| NAME-07 | **Group by, sort by, index by produce them.** The operations that produce those shapes are `_group_by_`, `_sort_by_` and `_index_by_`. The criterion follows the verb. | <pre>users_index_by_id(users)     // user_by_id<br>users_group_by_role(users)   // users_by_role<br>items_sort_by_time(items)    // items_sorted_by_time</pre> ![users_index_by_id() makes user_by_id, users_group_by_role() makes users_by_role, items_sort_by_time() makes items_sorted_by_time](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/group_sort_index_by.svg) | [docs/README.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/docs/README.md) |
| NAME-08 | **"From" means computed: result first, source last.** Use `_from_` only when something is computed, parsed or constructed — result first, source last. | <pre>user_from_token(token)<br>date_from_timestamp(ts)<br>tree_from_array(rows)</pre> ![a token is parsed into a User: user_from_token, the result first and the source last](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/from_means_computed.svg) | [docs/README.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/docs/README.md) |
| NAME-09 | **`_from_` never means lookup.** A lookup disguised as construction is wrong. | <pre>user_from_id(id)   ✗ wrong<br>user_by_id&#91;id]     ✓ right</pre> ![an id looked up in the user_by_id table: user_by_id[id] is right, user_from_id(id) dresses the lookup as construction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/from_is_not_lookup.svg) | [naming_markers.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/naming_markers.md) |
| NAME-10 | **"To" belongs in method position.** A standalone conversion prefers `_from_`; `_to_` is for method position, where the source is the receiver. | `tree.to_json()` ![tree.to_json() with tree as the receiver; standalone it is json_from_tree(tree), never tree_to_json(tree)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/to_in_method_position.svg) | [naming_markers.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/naming_markers.md) |
| NAME-11 | **No "to" in data names.** `_to_` is banned in data names — `id_to_name` is only a second spelling of `name_by_id`. | <pre>id_to_name    ✗ banned<br>name_by_id    ✓ right</pre> ![a map from ids to names is name_by_id; id_to_name is a second name for the same map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/no_to_in_data.svg) | [naming_markers.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/naming_markers.md) |
| NAME-12 | **No "indexed by"; bare "by" says it.** `_indexed_by_` does not exist. Bare `_by_` already names that shape. | <pre>users_indexed_by_id   ✗ does not exist<br>user_by_id            ✓ right</pre> ![users_index_by_id() makes user_by_id; users_indexed_by_id does not exist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/no_indexed_by.svg) | [naming_markers.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/naming_markers.md) |
| NAME-13 | **"Grouped by" only for invariant plurals.** `_grouped_by_` is retired from data names except for invariant plurals — `fish`, `data`, `series` — which cannot state cardinality by plurality. Prefer a countable noun when one exists. | <pre>fish_by_tank           // Record&lt;tank, Fish&gt;<br>fish_grouped_by_tank   // Record&lt;tank, Fish&#91;]&gt;<br>rows_by_source         ✓ over data_by_source</pre> ![fish_by_tank returns one Fish, fish_grouped_by_tank a list; rows_by_source is preferred over data_by_source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/grouped_by_invariant_plurals.svg) | [var_names.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/var_names.md) |
| NAME-14 | **"Of" queries possession.** `_of_` is a possession query. | `descendants_of(node)` ![a node and its five descendants in a tree, asked for as descendants_of(node)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/of_queries_possession.svg) | [naming_markers.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/naming_markers.md) |
| NAME-15 | **"is" names a boolean, a predicate or data.** `is_` names a boolean: a predicate that returns one, or data that holds one. It is not a function marker; a check that must read as a call is `check_*`, a verb. | <pre>is_ancestor(a, b)   // a predicate, called<br>is_open             // a boolean, read<br>check_status()      // a check that reads as a call</pre> ![is_ancestor(a, b) is called and returns true, is_open is read as false, check_status() is a verb that runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/is_names_a_boolean.svg) | [naming_markers.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/naming_markers.md) |
| NAME-16 | **A conversion and its variable share a first word.** A standalone conversion and the variable it fills share their first word. | `const json = json_from_tree(tree);` ![const json = json_from_tree(tree): the variable and the conversion share the word json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/conversion_shares_first_word.svg) | [naming_markers.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/naming_markers.md) |
| NAME-17 | **Names start with the domain.** Naming is domain-first. Functions and files follow `items_*`, `item_*` or domain nouns; generic names are avoided. | <pre>items_index_by_uid()   ✓ right<br>process() handle() util()   ✗ avoid</pre> ![domain-first names such as items_sort_by_time() stand together; handle(), process() and util() say nothing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/domain_first.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| NAME-18 | **Verb-first families are the exceptions.** The verb-first families are the exceptions to domain-first naming: `main` — reserved for the entry function of an executable script — `format_*`, `render_*`, `export_*`, `is_*`, `refresh_*`, `click_*`, `emit_*`, `check_*` (MP-40), `make_*` (MP-53), and the steps of a script (`build_glossaries_html()`). A step is a function `main()` calls once per part of the work, in order; a verb-first name that is not a step is renamed when next touched. | <pre>function main()<br>{<br>    report_print();<br>}</pre> ![main, format_*, render_*, export_*, is_*, refresh_*, click_*, emit_*, check_* and make_* start with their verb; main runs the steps of a script](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/verb_first_families.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| **VAR** | **Variables** — A name states the shape of its data. | | |
| VAR-01 | **A variable name states the shape of its data.** | <pre>users                  // User&#91;]<br>user_by_id             // Record&lt;id, User&gt;<br>users_by_role          // Record&lt;role, User&#91;]&gt;<br>items_sorted_by_time   // Item&#91;], reordered</pre> ![Four names and the shapes they state: users a list, user_by_id one User per id, users_by_role a list per role, items_sorted_by_time the same list reordered](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_shape_in_the_name.svg) | [var_names.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/var_names.md) |
| VAR-02 | **Name the result out.** A variable the function builds and returns unchanged is named `out` — `return out;`, exactly. A parameter, a loop variable or an outer value returned unchanged keeps its own name: `return user;`. | <pre>function emails_from_users(users)<br>{<br>    const out = &#91;];<br>    for (const user of users) {<br>        if (user.email) {<br>            out.push(user.email);<br>        }<br>    }<br>    return out;<br>}</pre> ![emails_from_users builds out, pushes into it and returns out; returning a parameter unchanged as out is wrong, return user; is right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_out_is_the_built_result.svg) | [return_out.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/return_out.md) |
| VAR-03 | **`out` never leaves the function.** The caller names the result by what it means. | <pre>const emails = emails_from_users(users);<br>const users_by_role = users_group_by_role(users);</pre> ![Inside emails_from_users the result is out; the caller names it emails](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_out_stays_inside.svg) | [return_out.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/return_out.md) |
| VAR-04 | **Return a literal directly.** Returning a literal or an expression directly is allowed; a guard return may return `null`, `false`, `[]`, `{}`. `const out = {...}; return out;` is rewritten as `return {...};` | <pre>const out = {a, b};<br>return out;          ✗ rewrite this<br><br>return {a, b};       ✓ as this</pre> ![const out = {a, b}; return out; rewritten as return {a, b};, and the guard returns null, false, () and {}](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_return_a_literal.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| VAR-05 | **Errors use e in arrows, error in regular handlers.** A caught error is `error` in a catch binding or regular function, and `e` in an arrow. This applies to promise rejection handlers and EventEmitter error listeners. Callback names stay `e` / `error` at every depth. DOM error events follow VAR-16; only nested catch bindings use numbered names (VAR-17). | <pre>promise.catch(e =&gt; report(e));<br><br>server.on('error', function (error) {<br>    throw error;<br>});<br><br>catch (error) {<br>    console.log(error.message);<br>}</pre> ![An error is e in an arrow, error in a regular function and in a catch binding](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_errors_e_and_error.svg) | [var_names_error.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/var_names_error.md) |
| VAR-06 | **Reserve e for error arrows; no err or ex.** `e` names an arrow error parameter. A regular error parameter or catch binding uses `error`, never `e`, `err` or `ex`; only catch bindings get the nested numbers in VAR-17. | <pre>catch (e)     ✗ no<br>catch (err)   ✗ no<br>catch (error) ✓ yes<br><br>promise.catch(e =&gt; report(e));   ✓ yes</pre> ![catch (err), catch (ex) and catch (e) each rewritten as catch (error); e only in an error arrow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_no_err_or_ex.svg) | [var_names_error.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/var_names_error.md) |
| VAR-07 | **Name stderr text by what it is.** Accumulated stderr text is not an error variable. Name it by what it is. | <pre>stderr   ✓ right<br>err      ✗ wrong</pre> ![A child process writes stderr text, collected as stderr, not as err](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_stderr_by_what_it_is.svg) | [var_names_error.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/var_names_error.md) |
| VAR-08 | **Prefer explicit temporaries.** Use intermediate variables instead of nested expressions; favor clarity over terseness. | ![A nested send(format_report(rows_filter(...))) rewritten as three named steps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_explicit_temporaries.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| VAR-09 | **Arrow values use v; arrow errors use e.** A lone value or event parameter is `v`; `vv` only when `v` is already taken where the arrow stands, `vvv` only when `vv` is. An arrow with no parameter, an error arrow or a parameter with another name takes nothing: `() => items.filter(v => v.ok)`, `promise.catch(e => report(e, items.map(v => v.uid)))`. A parameter the arrow does not use is not declared: `promise.catch(() => items.map(v => v.uid))`, not `e => …` (LINT-03); a regular function may. Error arrows keep `e` at every depth (VAR-05). With several parameters, choose names for their roles; an error callback’s first parameter still follows the error naming rule. | <pre>items.map(v =&gt; v.uid)<br>items.some(v =&gt; v.sizes.some(vv =&gt; vv.width &gt; 100))<br>promise.catch(e =&gt; report(e))</pre> ![Nested arrows name their value v, then vv only when v is taken, then vvv; an error arrow keeps e](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_arrows_v_and_e.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| VAR-10 | **The `for...of` loop variable is the singular of the collection.** | <pre>for (const user of users) { }<br>for (const child of node.children) { }</pre> ![users gives user and node.children gives child; for (const x of users) rewritten as for (const user of users)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_for_of_singular.svg) | [for_of.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/for_of.md) |
| VAR-11 | **A cached length is "end".** A cached array length in a single loop is named `end`. | <pre>for (let i = 0, end = items.length; i &lt; end; ++i) {<br>}</pre> ![Six items, the index i and the cached bound end = 6, in for (let i = 0, end = items.length; i < end; ++i)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_cached_length_end.svg) | [for_i_end_ii_jj_kk.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/for_i_end_ii_jj_kk.md) |
| VAR-12 | **Nested bounds double the index: ii, jj, kk.** In nested loops the cached bound is the doubled index name: i → ii, j → jj, k → kk. | <pre>for (let i = 0, ii = foo.length; i &lt; ii; ++i) {<br>    for (let j = 0, jj = bar.length; j &lt; jj; ++j) {<br>        for (let k = 0, kk = baz.length; k &lt; kk; ++k) {<br>        }<br>    }<br>}</pre> ![Three nested loops: i with ii, j with jj, k with kk, each bound its index doubled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_nested_bounds_doubled.svg) | [for_i_end_ii_jj_kk.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/for_i_end_ii_jj_kk.md) |
| VAR-13 | **A transformed or conditional result is not "out".** Only that variable is `out`. A value that is joined, stringified or otherwise transformed on its way out, or returned only on a condition (`?:`, `if`), is not `out`; it is named by what it is. | ![out returned on a condition and out joined on its way out, each beside the same code with a name of its own; below, the one right shape: built, then return out;](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/drafts/return-out.png) | [return_out.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/return_out.md) |
| VAR-14 | **Start time is "time0".** The variable holding the start time of a measurement is always named `time0`. The elapsed time is the current time minus `time0`: a number, shown to a person only through `format_duration` (FN-02), never as `${Date.now() - time0}ms` at the call site. | <pre>$time0 = microtime(true);<br>echo format_duration(microtime(true) - $time0);<br><br>const time0 = Date.now();<br>console.log(format_duration(Date.now() - time0));</pre> ![time0, the work, Date.now() - time0, then format_duration gives 2m 35s; a hand-rolled ms string rewritten as format_duration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_time0_start.svg) | [var_names_time0.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/var_names_time0.md) |
| VAR-15 | **Use time0 for measurement; paired names for other roles.** Do not name an elapsed-time start `begin`, `start` or `t0`. Outside that role, use `start/finish` or `begin/end` when the pair is actually used. | <pre>const time0 = Date.now();  // elapsed-time measurement<br><br>const start = range.start;<br>const finish = range.finish;</pre> ![A measurement start named start rewritten as time0; a range keeps start and finish or begin and end](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_time0_vs_pairs.svg) | [var_names_time0.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/var_names_time0.md) |
| VAR-16 | **Events use v in arrows, event in regular functions.** A DOM event is a value, including an event whose type is `error`. A one-parameter arrow uses `v`; a regular event handler uses `event`. Reserve `e` for error values in arrows. | <pre>el.addEventListener('click', v =&gt; v.stopPropagation());<br>el.addEventListener('error', v =&gt; report(v));<br><br>el.addEventListener('error', function (event) {<br>    report(event);<br>});</pre> ![A click or error event is v in an arrow and event in a regular function](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_events_v_and_event.svg) | [var_names_event.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/var_names_event.md) |
| VAR-17 | **Nested catch bindings use error2, error3.** A catch inside another catch names its binding `error2`, the next level `error3`. This applies only to catch bindings: callback parameters stay `e` in arrows and `error` in regular functions, even inside a catch. | <pre>catch (error) {<br>    try {<br>        await save_backup(scene);<br>    }<br>    catch (error2) {<br>    }<br>}</pre> ![A catch inside a catch binds error2, the next error3; callbacks stay e or error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_nested_catch_numbered.svg) | [var_names_event.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/var_names_event.md) |
| VAR-18 | **A generic name has one meaning.** `i`, `j`, `k`, `end`, `ii`, `v`, `e`, `error`, `event`, `out`, `time0`, `req`, `res` and `rej` each have the meaning listed on one page, `res` one in each of its pairs, `req/res` and `res/rej`; anywhere else the variable is named by what it holds. | <pre>const out = &#91;...new Set(tags)];<br>return (out.length === tags.length) ? tags : out;   ✗ no<br><br>const unique_tags = &#91;...new Set(tags)];<br>return (unique_tags.length === tags.length) ? tags : unique_tags;   ✓ yes</pre> ![The generic names and their meanings, res in both its pairs; out returned on a condition rewritten as unique_tags](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_generic_name_one_meaning.svg) | [generic_names.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/generic_names.md) |
| VAR-19 | **A configuration value at the top is UPPER_CASE.** A constant the module keeps as configuration, a global name for a value set in the code, is written in upper case at the module's top level. A `const` inside a function or a block is lower case. Imports are not this rule. | <pre>const PRESS_MS = 400;           // the module's top<br><br>function press_start(event)<br>{<br>    const started = Date.now();  // inside<br>}</pre> ![PRESS_MS and BLOB_URL at the module's top in upper case; started and target inside a function in lower case](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/var_config_upper_case.svg) | [MANUALLY_APPROVED_RULES.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/MANUALLY_APPROVED_RULES.md) |
| **FN** | **Function contracts** — What a prefix promises the caller. | | |
| FN-01 | **"format" strictly returns human-facing text.** `format_*` returns a string to show to a person, including when the value comes from object state. | <pre>format_bytes(1457664)    // "1.4 MB"<br>format_duration(155000)  // "2m 35s"<br>format_usd(1299)         // "$12.99"</pre> ![format_bytes, format_duration and format_usd turn values into the strings a person reads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fn_format_human_text.svg) | [format_xxx.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/format_xxx.md) |
| FN-05 | **"render" constructs asset content.** `render_*` constructs content such as CSS, HTML or SVG from state. The result can be a string; its purpose is an asset rather than a human-facing formatted value. | <pre>public function render_css(): string<br>{<br>    return "body { color: {$this-&gt;text_color}; }";<br>}</pre> ![render_css and render_svg turn state into CSS and SVG assets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fn_render_constructs_assets.svg) | [render_xxx.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/render_xxx.md) |
| FN-02 | **Never hand-roll a display conversion.** A display conversion is never hand-rolled at a call site — an inline one is a missed `format_*`. | <pre>${Math.round(bytes / 1024)}kB   ✗ missed call<br>format_bytes(bytes)             ✓ right</pre> ![Three hand-rolled byte conversions giving three answers, each rewritten as format_bytes(b) giving 1.4 MB](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fn_no_hand_rolled_display.svg) | [format_xxx.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/format_xxx.md) |
| FN-03 | **`format_*` returns — it never prints.** Output is the caller’s job. | `console.log(format_tree(tree));` ![format_tree returns the text and the caller prints it; a format_tree that prints rewritten as console.log(format_tree(tree))](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fn_format_returns.svg) | [format_xxx.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/format_xxx.md) |
| FN-04 | **"format" is not serialization.** `format_*` is not for machine formats. Serialization is conversion, not display. | <pre>format_user(user)     // "Alex K. (admin)" — humans<br>json_from_user(user)  // machines</pre> ![format_user gives the text a person reads; json_from_user gives the JSON a machine reads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fn_format_not_serialization.svg) | [format_xxx.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/format_xxx.md) |
| FN-06 | **"render" is recomputed, never stored.** The prefix separates constructed content from stored attributes. `render_*` is recomputed per call — never cached, never stored. | <pre>$this-&gt;text_color     // stored attribute<br>$this-&gt;render_css()   // constructed content</pre> ![A stored attribute is read; render_css is made on each call; storing its result rewritten as calling it where needed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fn_render_recomputed.svg) | [render_xxx.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/render_xxx.md) |
| FN-07 | **"render" may return null or throw.** `render_*` may return `null` when not applicable, and may throw when the state makes the value meaningless. | <pre>if (!$this-&gt;theme) {<br>    return null;<br>}</pre> ![render_css returns CSS for a theme, null with no theme, and throws for a broken one](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fn_render_null_or_throw.svg) | [render_xxx.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/render_xxx.md) |
| FN-08 | **"render" is sync and pure; downloads are "export".** `render_*` constructs content without DOM updates, file writes or downloads, and always returns its result. A function that brings a part of the page up to date returns nothing and is `refresh_<what>` (FN-10), never `<what>_render`. A downloadable artifact — zip, csv or xlsx — is `export_*`, which may be async and side-effectful. | <pre>$theme-&gt;render_css()    // construct CSS content<br>refresh_theme_labels()  // bring a part of the page up to date<br>export_zip()            // produce a downloadable artifact</pre> ![render_css returns CSS, refresh_theme_labels updates the page, export_zip makes a download; theme_labels_render rewritten as refresh_theme_labels](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fn_render_refresh_export.svg) | [render_xxx.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/render_xxx.md) |
| FN-09 | **Format and render differ by output purpose.** `format_*` returns a string a person reads; `render_*` constructs asset content. Both may return strings; reading object state does not turn display text into render output. | <pre>format_bytes(1457664)   // "1.4 MB", human-facing text<br>$theme-&gt;render_css()   // CSS asset content</pre> ![format_bytes returns text a person reads; render_css returns CSS a browser uses](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fn_format_vs_render.svg) | [format_xxx.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/format_xxx.md) |
| FN-10 | **A local copy of remote data has "refresh".** Anything that holds a local copy of remote data has `refresh()` — it pulls the data and brings the local vars up to date. Mental model: the browser refresh button. | <pre>refresh: async function () {<br>    await Promise.all(&#91;<br>        this.refresh_user(),<br>        this.refresh_photos(),<br>    ]);<br>},</pre> ![refresh pulls the remote data into the local copy, this.user and this.photos](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fn_refresh_local_copy.svg) | [refresh.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/refresh.md) |
| FN-11 | **Refresh is safe to call anytime.** `refresh()` is idempotent — safe to call at any moment, any number of times. | ![refresh called on load, after a save and twice in a row reaches the same up-to-date state](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fn_refresh_idempotent.svg) | [refresh.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/refresh.md) |
| FN-12 | **Refresh composes per-part refreshes.** A fine-grained `refresh_<part>()` syncs one part of the state; `refresh()` composes them. | <pre>refresh_user: async function () {<br>    this.user = await fetch_user();<br>},</pre> ![refresh runs refresh_user and refresh_photos, each filling its own part](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fn_refresh_composes_parts.svg) | [refresh.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/refresh.md) |
| FN-13 | **Init is the first refresh.** | <pre>mounted: async function () {<br>    await this.refresh();<br>    this.ready = true;<br>},</pre> ![mounted awaits this.refresh(), then sets this.ready = true](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fn_init_is_first_refresh.svg) | [refresh.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/refresh.md) |
| FN-14 | **A modal returns a commit flag.** An interaction — modal, popover — executes its own logic and returns a boolean commit flag. It expresses intent; it does not expose control flow. These are the best practices for vue-modal: `modal.return(true)` inside, `await modal_x().promise()` at the call site. | <pre>// true  → changes were committed<br>// false → no-op (cancel, or no changes)<br>if (await modal_upload().promise()) {<br>    await blocking(this.refresh());<br>}</pre> ![The caller awaits modal_upload; the modal does its own work and returns true, committed, or false, nothing to do](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fn_modal_returns_a_flag.svg) | [interactions-should-return-only-boolean-flag.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/interactions-should-return-only-boolean-flag.md) |
| FN-15 | **Guards return early.** Validate inputs immediately and return `null` or empty values explicitly. | ![The work buried in nested ifs rewritten as guards that return null and () first](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fn_guards_return_early.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FN-16 | **One public value per library module.** A reusable module exports one function, class, configuration or data value. Executable scripts export nothing; tool-shaped files follow the tool. | ![format_bytes.js, Theme.js and config.js export one value each, bin/build exports nothing; a helpers.js exporting three values split into three modules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fn_one_value_per_module.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| **FMT** | **Formatting** — Braces, breaks, blank lines, comments. | | |
| FMT-01 | **Four spaces, no tabs.** Indentation is exactly 4 spaces. No tabs. | ![A tab before const user turned into four spaces, shown as dots](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_four_spaces.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-02 | **A top-level function declaration puts its opening brace on the next line.** | <pre>function main()<br>{<br>}</pre> ![function main() { with the brace on its line, turned into the brace on the next line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_top_level_brace_below.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-03 | **Nested function: brace on the same line.** A function declared inside another function keeps its opening brace on the declaration line. | <pre>function main()<br>{<br>    function limit_print(limit) {<br>    }<br>}</pre> ![limit_print nested in main: its brace moves from a line of its own to the declaration line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_nested_brace_inline.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-04 | **Callbacks keep the brace on the line.** Function expressions, callbacks and Promise executors keep the opening brace on the declaration line. | <pre>server.on('error', function (error) {<br>    // ...<br>});<br><br>return new Promise(function (resolve, reject) {<br>    // ...<br>});</pre> ![A callback and a Promise executor with the brace below, turned into the brace on the declaration line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_callback_brace_inline.svg) | [formatting_blocks.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/formatting_blocks.md) |
| FMT-05 | **Class brace below; method brace inline.** A class declaration puts its brace on the next line; its methods keep the brace on the declaration line. | <pre>class Logger<br>{<br>    constructor(parent_group_uid) {<br>    }<br><br>    write(format, ...values) {<br>    }<br>}</pre> ![class Logger with its brace inline and a method brace below, turned into the class brace below and the method brace inline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_class_brace_below.svg) | [formatting_blocks.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/formatting_blocks.md) |
| FMT-07 | **Always use braces.** Always use braces for `if`, `else`, `for`, `while`. No single-line bodies. | <pre>if (!user) return null;   ✗ no<br><br>if (!user) {              ✓ yes<br>    return null;<br>}</pre> ![if (!user) return null; on one line, turned into the same body in braces](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_always_braces.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-08 | **`else` starts on a new line.** | <pre>if (a) {<br>}<br>else if (b) {<br>}<br>else {<br>}</pre> ![else glued to the closing brace, turned into else if and else each starting a line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_else_new_line.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-09 | **`catch` and `finally` start on a new line.** | <pre>try {<br>}<br>catch (error) {<br>}<br>finally {<br>}</pre> ![catch and finally glued to the closing braces, turned into each starting a line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_catch_new_line.svg) | [formatting_blocks.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/formatting_blocks.md) |
| FMT-10 | **Align "switch" and "case".** `switch` and `case` are aligned at the same indentation level. | <pre>switch (type) {<br>case 'voice':<br>    break;<br>case 'text':<br>    break;<br>default:<br>}</pre> ![case and default indented one level under switch, turned into aligned with switch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_switch_case_aligned.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-11 | **Keep short objects on one line; expand only when needed.** Multiple fields alone do not require line breaks. When size or nested structure requires a multi-line object literal, use one field per line and a trailing comma. | <pre>const next = {uid: item.uid, parent_uid: item.parent_uid, index};</pre> ![A short object broken over lines turned into one line, and an expanded object given its trailing comma](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_short_objects_one_line.svg) | [formatting_blocks.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/formatting_blocks.md) |
| FMT-12 | **Options-style methods are always function expressions.** Even a return-only method without its own `this` or `arguments` keeps that form; the tiny-arrow rule applies to callbacks and value factories. | <pre>const options = {<br>    refresh: async function () {<br>    },<br>    px: function (value) {<br>        return value ? `${value}px` : '0';<br>    },<br>};</pre> ![An options object with arrow methods, turned into the same methods written as function expressions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_options_methods_function.svg) | [formatting_blocks.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/formatting_blocks.md) |
| FMT-13 | **Keep an expression on one line when it fits on one line.** | ![const total broken over two lines, turned into one line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_expression_one_line.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-14 | **Never break after "=" before a call.** Never split an assignment after `=` when its right-hand side is a single function call. | <pre>const users_by_role =<br>    users_group_by_role(users);   ✗ no<br><br>const users_by_role = users_group_by_role(users);   ✓ yes</pre> ![const user = with the call on the next line, turned into one line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_no_break_after_equals.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-15 | **Break lines only to show structure.** Break a statement only when its size or nested structure makes the break necessary. Line breaks must expose structure. | ![A short condition broken for nothing turned into one line; a list of rows broken one row a line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_breaks_show_structure.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-16 | **A blank line marks a phase change — nothing else.** Add one only when the following statement begins an independent conceptual step. | ![Blank lines after every statement, turned into one blank line before the printing step](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_blank_line_phase.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-17 | **Keep setup next to its use.** Keep setup adjacent to the loop, condition or call that immediately uses it. Tightly coupled setup and use are not separated merely because the statement type changes. | ![const lines = () separated from its loop by a blank line, turned into right above it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_setup_next_to_use.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-18 | **Build objects from needed fields only.** Construct an object from the required fields only. Do not spread a full object when a subset is needed. | <pre>{...item, index}                              ✗ bad<br>{uid: item.uid, parent_uid: item.parent_uid, index}   ✓ good</pre> ![An object built by spreading the whole item, turned into one that names uid and index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_object_needed_fields.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-19 | **Comment intent, not mechanics.** Comments explain intent or policy only. No comments for obvious mechanics. One exception: the route comment of FMT-21 states the route. | ![A comment repeating the call, turned into one giving the reason for the retry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_comment_intent.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-20 | **Multi-line comments carry rules or guarantees.** A multi-line comment carries a rule, an invariant or a guarantee. | ![A three-line comment retelling the steps, turned into a two-line limit the function keeps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_multiline_comment_rule.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-21 | **Every route has a route comment.** Every route function carries a route comment directly above it: `METHOD /path (params)`. | <pre>// Express route handler<br>// GET /file/&lt;name&gt;<br>async function file_get(req, res)<br>{<br>}</pre> ![A route function with no comment, turned into one with its route comment, GET /file/<name>](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_route_comment.svg) | [endpoint_comment.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/endpoint_comment.md) |
| FMT-22 | **Parentheses only when the route takes input.** Parentheses appear only when the endpoint takes input — body, headers, query, comma-separated, in that order. | <pre>// Express route handler<br>// POST /upload (body, header:x-filename)<br>function upload_post(req, res)<br>{<br>}</pre> ![GET /health () losing its empty parentheses, and the upload route listing body before its header](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_route_params.svg) | [endpoint_comment.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/endpoint_comment.md) |
| FMT-23 | **Headers prefixed; path params in the path.** A header is prefixed with `header:`; a path parameter is spelled in the path itself. | <pre>header:x-filename<br>/file/&lt;name&gt;</pre> ![GET /file (name, x-token) turned into GET /file/<name> (header:x-token)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_route_header_prefix.svg) | [endpoint_comment.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/endpoint_comment.md) |
| FMT-24 | **An intent comment continues the same block on the next line.** | <pre>// POST /upload (body, header:x-filename)<br>// Streams to data/ before the body is fully read.</pre> ![An intent comment split from the route comment by a blank line, turned into the next line of the same block](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_intent_comment_continues.svg) | [endpoint_comment.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/endpoint_comment.md) |
| FMT-25 | **Named functions outside class bodies are "function" declarations.** Every named function outside a class — top-level or nested — is a `function name(...)` declaration. Class methods use their class syntax. | <pre>function report_print()<br>{<br>}</pre> ![A function expression and an arrow held in const report_print, each turned into a function declaration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_named_function_declaration.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-26 | **No spaces inside one-line braces.** A single-line object or array literal has no space inside its braces or brackets — a standalone literal, a nested one, or one row of a list. | <pre>{ value: 'today', label: 'Today' }   ✗ no<br>{value: 'today', label: 'Today'}     ✓ yes<br><br>&#91; 'remote', 'host', 'service' ]     ✗ no<br>&#91;'remote', 'host', 'service']       ✓ yes</pre> ![An object and an array with spaces inside their braces, turned into the same with none](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_no_spaces_in_braces.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-27 | **Parenthesize compound operands in logic.** In a logical expression (`&&`, `\|\|`, `??`) and in the condition of a ternary, an operand that carries an operator of its own is wrapped in parentheses. A simple operand — identifier, member access, call, template literal, unary negation — stays bare, and a chain of one logical operator is one expression. A ternary given whole — a value, an argument, a return — stays bare too: it is wrapped only as an operand of another operator. A Vue directive keeps its parentheses (VUE-06), and only a directive: a condition moved out of a `v-if` into a computed or a method loses them. | <pre>return is_dev &#124;&#124; i === end - 1;     ✗ no<br>return is_dev &#124;&#124; (i === end - 1);   ✓ yes<br><br>return (!is_ready &amp;&amp; !is_gone);   ✗ no<br>return !is_ready &amp;&amp; !is_gone;     ✓ yes<br><br>(state === 'done') ? 'ok' : 'wait'<br><br>url: (is_api ? '/api/v1' : null),   ✗ no<br>url: is_api ? '/api/v1' : null,     ✓ yes</pre> ![A comparison beside // and a ternary condition, each wrapped in parentheses, and a ternary or a chain given whole, bare](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_parenthesize_compound.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-28 | **One variable per declaration.** Each variable gets its own `const` or `let` statement; a declaration never lists several variables separated by commas. The header of an indexed loop is the exception. | <pre>const osc = c.createOscillator(),<br>    gain = c.createGain();          ✗ no<br><br>const osc = c.createOscillator();<br>const gain = c.createGain();        ✓ yes</pre> ![One const declaring osc and gain, turned into a const for each](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_one_variable_per_declaration.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-29 | **One blank line between top-level functions.** Top-level functions stand one blank line apart: each function declared at module level is followed by one blank line before the next one. | <pre>}<br>function toggle_sound()   ✗ no blank line<br><br>}<br><br>function toggle_sound()   ✓ one blank line</pre> ![Two top-level functions with no blank line between them, turned into one blank line apart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_blank_line_between_functions.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-30 | **Only the last argument spans lines.** Only the last argument of a call may span several lines; nothing follows a multi-line argument — no further argument after `}`, no chained call after `})`. A function that would leave arguments dangling is declared inside the caller and passed by name; a chained call becomes a variable. | <pre>page.evaluate(function (text) {<br>    // ...<br>}, text);                          ✗ dangling<br><br>page.evaluate(find_families, text);   ✓ yes<br><br>items.filter(function (item) {<br>    // ...<br>}).map(v =&gt; v.uid);               ✗ dangling</pre> ![A call with an argument after its multi-line function, and a call chained after one, each rewritten so nothing dangles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_last_argument_spans.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-31 | **Build strings with template literals.** A string built from parts is a template literal; `+` never joins a string to a value. Plain quotes stay for a one-line string with nothing to interpolate; a string that spans lines is a template literal (SQL-01). | <pre>'weapons/turret-' + weapon.id    ✗ no<br>&#96;weapons/turret-${weapon.id}&#96;    ✓ yes</pre> !['weapons/turret-' + weapon.id turned into a template literal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_template_literals.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FMT-32 | **An empty function is `{}` on one line.** An empty function expression or arrow is a no-op, as `ignore` is: its body is `{}` on one line, never split over two. A function declaration and a method keep their braces on lines of their own; a body holding only a comment is not empty. | <pre>params.update = params.update \|\| function () {<br>};                                                ✗ no<br><br>params.update = params.update \|\| function () {};   ✓ yes<br>promise.catch(() =&gt; {});                          ✓ yes</pre> ![An empty function expression split over two lines, turned into {} on one line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/fmt_empty_function_one_line.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| **FLOW** | **Control flow** — Imperative, explicit, no magic. | | |
| FLOW-01 | **Prefer imperative control flow.** | ![A loop that keeps the uids of active items, beside its four steps in the order they run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/flow_imperative.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FLOW-02 | **No index needed: use for...of.** Prefer `for...of` when the index is not needed. | <pre>for (const item of items) {<br>}</pre> ![An indexed loop that only fetches items(i), turned into for (const item of items)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/flow_for_of.svg) | [for_of.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/for_of.md) |
| FLOW-03 | **Use an indexed loop when the index is needed.** | <pre>for (let i = 0, end = items.length; i &lt; end; ++i) {<br>}</pre> ![Five items with their indexes: items(i) and items(i + 1) read together, so the loop counts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/flow_indexed_loop.svg) | [for_of.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/for_of.md) |
| FLOW-04 | **No do...while.** `do { ... } while (...)` does not exist. Use `while` or `for`. | ![do...while with its condition at the bottom, turned into while with the condition first](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/flow_no_do_while.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FLOW-05 | **Reduce and chains only on one line.** `reduce`, deep chaining and functional pipelines are allowed only if the entire expression fits on a single line. | ![A one-line reduce kept; a four-line filter, map and reduce chain turned into a loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/flow_chains_one_line.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FLOW-06 | **Arrows only for tiny callbacks.** Do not use arrow functions for non-trivial logic. Arrows are allowed only for tiny callbacks. | <pre>const uids = items.map(v =&gt; v.uid);<br>fresh.catch(ignore);</pre> ![An arrow holding a conditional computation, turned into a named function; tiny arrows kept](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/flow_arrows_tiny.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FLOW-07 | **A block-body arrow becomes a function.** An arrow with a block body does not exist — it becomes `function (...) {}`, with an optional `_this` inside. The empty `() => {}`, a no-op, is the one exception (FMT-32). | <pre>request.on('end', async () =&gt; {          ✗ does not exist<br>});<br><br>request.on('end', async function () {     ✓ this<br>});</pre> ![An async arrow with a block body, turned into async function; the empty () => {} is the exception](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/flow_block_arrow_function.svg) | [formatting_blocks.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/formatting_blocks.md) |
| FLOW-08 | **A `catch` that ignores the error binds nothing.** | <pre>try {<br>}<br>catch {<br>}</pre> ![catch (error) with error never read, turned into catch {}](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/flow_catch_binds_nothing.svg) | [formatting_blocks.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/formatting_blocks.md) |
| FLOW-09 | **Plain data: Set, Map or {}.** Use plain data structures — `Set`, `Map` or plain `{}` for lookups. No prototypes, no mutation via shared state. A module may own its state, a singleton over its own data, written only by its own functions; shared means across modules, and that is what is forbidden. | <pre>let modal = null;    // the module's own<br><br>function modal_show()<br>{<br>    modal = modal_make();<br>}</pre> ![Set, Map and {} for lookups; another module writing modal state, turned into a module writing only its own](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/flow_plain_data.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FLOW-10 | **No implicit magic or hidden side effects.** No implicit magic. No hidden side effects, no reliance on execution-order side effects. The one visible exception: side-effect imports, which sit at the very top of the file, in the order they run (FILE-11). | <pre>import './sass/main.sass';   // the top of the file, in run order<br>import './main-pre';<br><br>import Vue from 'vue';</pre> ![A side-effect import hidden mid-list, moved to the top block in run order](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/flow_no_hidden_effects.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FLOW-11 | **A return-only callback is an arrow.** Options-style methods retain function expressions (FMT-12). A callback whose body is only `return <expression>`, and whose arrow fits on one line, is written as that arrow — the mirror of FLOW-07. `function` stays for a callback that does more, or that needs `this` or `arguments`. | <pre>items.filter(function (item) {<br>    return item_text(item) === text;<br>});                                       ✗ no<br><br>items.filter(v =&gt; item_text(v) === text);   ✓ yes</pre> ![A filter callback that only returns, turned from a function into an arrow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/flow_return_only_arrow.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FLOW-12 | **Names are written whole.** A constant, function, method, class or property is never glued together from strings at run time; a search or a rename must find it. A value that picks one of a few known names lists them with `match` (PHP) or `switch` (JavaScript). A name built at run time only for an open set that cannot be listed. | <pre>constant(Invoice::class.'::STATUS_'.strtoupper($status))   ✗ no<br><br>match ($status) {                                          ✓ yes<br>    'paid' =&gt; Invoice::STATUS_PAID,<br>    'void' =&gt; Invoice::STATUS_VOID,<br>}</pre> ![A search for STATUS_PAID misses a name glued at run time and finds it in a match that lists it whole](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/flow_names_whole.svg) | [names_written_whole.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/names_written_whole.md) |
| **FILE** | **File and module structure** — One entry function, one fixed order. | | |
| FILE-01 | **A library module exports one public value last.** The value may be a function, class, configuration or data. Declare it above and export its name at file end; tool-shaped files follow their tool. | `module.exports = items_index_by_uid;` ![A library file: requires, the value, helpers, and module.exports of that one value last](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_one_export_last.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FILE-02 | **A script runs main and exports nothing.** An executable script uses `main` as its entry function and does not export. | ![A script that exports, turned into one that only runs: shebang, requires, cli(main), main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_script_runs_main.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FILE-03 | **Library or executable, never both.** Do not combine a library export and an executable invocation in the same file. | ![A file that both exports and runs, split into a library and an executable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_library_or_executable.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FILE-04 | **An executable hands main to cli.** An executable hands its entry function to `cli`. `cli` owns the process contract: it keeps the event loop alive until `main` settles, reports a failure, and exits non-zero — `ExitCodeError` picks the code, any other error exits 1. A browser page script has no `cli`; it calls `main();` (MP-10). | <pre>const cli = require('@vbarbarosh/node-helpers/src/cli');<br><br>cli(main);<br><br>async function main()<br>{<br>}</pre> ![main handed to cli, which keeps the loop alive, reports a failure and exits non-zero](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_cli_owns_exit.svg) | [cli_main.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/cli_main.md) |
| FILE-05 | **`cli(main)`, never `cli(main())`.** `cli` runs the function through `Promise.try`, so a synchronous throw is reported like a rejection; an already-invoked `main()` is a promise, and `Promise.try` rejects it with “expecting a function” — the app dies at startup. | <pre>cli(main);     ✓ right<br>cli(main());   ✗ dies at startup</pre> ![cli(main()) hands cli a promise and dies at startup; cli(main) lets cli call main and report a throw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_cli_main_not_called.svg) | [cli_main.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/cli_main.md) |
| FILE-06 | **No hand-rolled catch and exit.** A hand-rolled `main().catch(...)` with `process.exit(1)` does not exist. | <pre>main().catch(function (error) {<br>    console.error(error);<br>    process.exit(1);<br>});                              ✗ does not exist</pre> ![A hand-written main().catch with process.exit(1), replaced by cli(main)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_no_hand_rolled_exit.svg) | [cli_main.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/cli_main.md) |
| FILE-07 | **Nothing precedes the shebang.** An executable script may start with a shebang; nothing may precede it. | `#!/usr/bin/env node` ![A comment above the shebang, moved below it so #! is line 1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_shebang_first.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FILE-08 | **Imports sorted in byte order.** The import block is sorted as plain text lines in byte order — what vim’s `:sort` over the block, or `LC_ALL=C sort`, produces. `require` and `import` alike. | <pre>const $ = require('jquery');<br>const Vue = require('vue');<br>const axios = require('axios');<br>const cli = require('@vbarbarosh/node-helpers/src/cli');<br>const fs = require('fs');<br>const {promisify} = require('util');</pre> ![Six requires in the order they were added, sorted in byte order as LC_ALL=C sort does](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_imports_byte_order.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FILE-09 | **The whole line is the sort key.** The whole line is the sort key — `const` or `import` included, not the module path and not the variable name. | ![Requires sorted by name ignoring case, re-sorted by the whole line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_whole_line_key.svg) | [imports_sorted.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/imports_sorted.md) |
| FILE-10 | **Byte order, not locale order.** Byte order, not locale order: `@` and `$` come before letters, uppercase before lowercase, and `{` after `z` — destructured imports land last. | <pre>const Vue = require('vue');       ← V before a<br>const axios = require('axios');<br>const {promisify} = require('util'); ← { after z</pre> ![Byte order: $ and @, then A to Z, a to z, then {; a locale-sorted list re-sorted that way](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_byte_not_locale.svg) | [imports_sorted.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/imports_sorted.md) |
| FILE-11 | **Imports form one unbroken list.** The import block is one contiguous list: no groups for builtins, packages and local files, and no blank lines or comments inside it — either one breaks the sort. Two exceptions: a side-effect import keeps its run order in its own block at the top, and the named imports (`{foo, bar}`) may stand apart after the default ones — one blank line between blocks. | <pre>import './sass/main.sass';<br>import './main-pre';<br><br>import Vue from 'vue';<br>import axios from 'axios';<br><br>import {mapState} from 'vuex';<br>import {promisify} from 'util';</pre> ![Imports split by comments into groups, turned into one list with side-effect and named blocks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_imports_one_list.svg) | [imports_sorted.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/imports_sorted.md) |
| FILE-12 | **Constants follow the requires.** File-level constants and variables follow the `require` statements. | `const REPORT_LIMIT = 31;` ![A constant above the requires, moved below them](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_constants_after_requires.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FILE-13 | **cli(main) right after initialization.** `cli(main);` comes immediately after all global initialization, and no executable code other than that call may appear before the public entry function. | ![Code run between cli(main) and main, turned into globals followed by cli(main)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_cli_main_after_init.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FILE-14 | **The public entry function is the first function in the file.** In an executable, the first function declaration is `function main()`. | ![A helper above main, moved below so main is the first function](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_entry_function_first.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FILE-15 | **Helpers follow the entry function.** Helpers are defined after the public entry function, and before a library’s final export. | ![A library file: the entry function, its helpers, then the export](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_helpers_after_entry.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FILE-16 | **Helpers must be named functions, not inline lambdas.** | ![A helper written as an arrow in a constant, turned into a named function](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_helpers_named.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FILE-17 | **This repository is CommonJS.** This repository's own code and node scripts are CommonJS: `const <name> = require('<module>');`, never `import` or `export`. Elsewhere the rules cover both module systems. | ![import and export default, turned into require and module.exports in this repository](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_commonjs.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FILE-18 | **Libraries follow a fixed order.** Library order is fixed. | `requires → constants → public entry → helpers → module.exports` ![The five parts of a library in order: requires, constants, entry, helpers, exports](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_library_order.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FILE-19 | **Executables follow a fixed order.** Executable order is fixed. | `shebang → requires → globals → cli(main); → main() → helpers` ![The six parts of a script in order: shebang, requires, globals, cli(main), main, helpers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_executable_order.svg) | [FORMATTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/FORMATTING.md) |
| FILE-20 | **One library export, last, and the file bears its name.** A reusable/library module exports one public value; the file is named after that value. Declare it above and export its name last: `module.exports = name;` or `export default name;`. Never combine an ES-module declaration with its export or export an inline expression. Executable scripts export nothing; tool-shaped files follow the tool. The tool decides the export's shape, never the file's name (MP-53). | <pre>// helper.js<br>function helper()<br>{<br>    return null;<br>}<br><br>export default helper;</pre> ![helper.js exporting a combined declaration or an inline expression, turned into helper declared, then exported by name](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_export_bears_name.svg) | [one_export_per_file.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/one_export_per_file.md) |
| FILE-21 | **No named exports; one public value per library module.** Several independent public functions are several modules, each named after its export. One exported class can contain methods. Several names are never taken from a local module. | <pre>export {engine_run, engine_transport};                   ✗ no<br>import {engine_run, engine_transport} from './engine';   ✗ no<br><br>import engine_run from './engine_run';                   ✓ yes<br>import engine_transport from './engine_transport';</pre> ![engine.js with two named exports, split into engine_run.js exporting one value](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_no_named_exports.svg) | [one_export_per_file.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/one_export_per_file.md) |
| FILE-23 | **Reusable scratch and test modules export one value too.** Research, scratch and test-support modules are not exempt. Executable scripts export nothing; tool-shaped files follow the tool. | ![A test fixtures module exporting two values, turned into users_fixture.js exporting one](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_scratch_one_export.svg) | [one_export_per_file.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/one_export_per_file.md) |
| FILE-24 | **Libraries and tools dictate their own shape.** A named import from a library is the library’s shape, and a file whose shape is dictated by a tool follows the tool — `module.exports.mochaHooks` in a mocha hooks file. | `import {mapState} from 'vuex';` ![vuex's named import and mocha's hooks file keep their tools' shape; a named import from a local module becomes one value](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_tools_dictate_shape.svg) | [one_export_per_file.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/one_export_per_file.md) |
| FILE-25 | **New code takes its place from its surroundings where no explicit rule applies.** Read the code around the insertion point — what stands together, in what order — and continue it within that scope. Explicit rules take priority (CORE-01); this does not require reorganizing existing code. | ![format_time appended after render_page, moved beside the other format_ functions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_place_from_surroundings.svg) | [new_code_placement.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/new_code_placement.md) |
| FILE-26 | **A function family stays unbroken.** A run of functions of one family — `render_*`, `format_*`, `click_*` — stays unbroken. A new member joins the run; a function of another family goes outside it, never between two members. | <pre>render_css()<br>describe()            ✗ splits the run<br>render_html()<br><br>render_css()<br>render_html()<br>describe()            ✓ after the run</pre> ![describe() between render_css and render_html, moved after the render run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/file_family_unbroken.svg) | [new_code_placement.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/new_code_placement.md) |
| **PROJ** | **Project layout** — A directory is a program; bin/ holds its verbs. | | |
| PROJ-01 | **One project shape; bin/ holds the verbs.** Every project keeps one shape. A directory is a program, and `bin/` holds its methods — one executable per verb, working the same in every language. | <pre>bin/build      bb<br>bin/configure<br>bin/release<br>bin/run        rr<br>bin/self-check<br>bin/test       tt<br>bin/watch      ww</pre> ![The bin/ folder with build, configure, release, run, self-check, test and watch, and the same verbs in a node.js, a python and a php project](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_bin_holds_the_verbs.svg) | [layout.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/layout.md) |
| PROJ-02 | **After git pull, run bin/configure.** `bin/configure` is the only command to run after `git pull` to make a checkout ready for development. | ![git pull, then bin/configure, then a checkout ready to work in; a list of remembered steps is replaced by that one command](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_configure_after_pull.svg) | [layout.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/layout.md) |
| PROJ-03 | **Run, test, build and watch wrap npm.** In a node.js project `run`, `test`, `build` and `watch` are usually thin wrappers over npm. The wrappers still earn their keep: `rr`, `tt`, `bb`, `ww` are shorter than any npm form, and the names hold for projects that are not node.js. | <pre>alias rr='bin/run'<br>alias tt='bin/test'<br>alias bb='bin/build'<br>alias ww='bin/watch'</pre> ![rr, tt, bb and ww call bin/run, bin/test, bin/build and bin/watch, which in a node.js project call npm start, npm test, npm run build and npm run watch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_wrappers_over_npm.svg) | [layout.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/layout.md) |
| PROJ-04 | **build/ is never committed; dist/ is the release.** `bin/build` puts what it builds into `build/`. `build/` is temporary: it and everything in it are never committed. Taking something out of it into the repository is a decision of its own, as `bin/release` does with `dist/`. `dist/` holds the released build, committed by `bin/release` at release time only. There is one build: `bin/release` runs it and copies `build/` into `dist/`. | <pre>build/   bin/build output, temporary, never committed<br>dist/    released build, committed by bin/release</pre> ![bin/build writes build/, never committed; bin/release runs the build and copies build/ into dist/, committed at release time only](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_build_and_dist.svg) | [layout.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/layout.md) |
| PROJ-05 | **Runtime state in data/, never committed.** `data/` holds runtime state. Never committed. | `data/logs/2026-08-24.txt` ![The running app writes data/logs/2026-08-24.txt; .gitignore lists data/, so git never sees it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_data_never_committed.svg) | [layout.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/layout.md) |
| PROJ-06 | **.env belongs to whoever runs the app.** `.env` is not the application's: docker loads it, or the Dockerfile sets the variables. The rules set nothing for it. | ![docker loads .env, or the Dockerfile sets the variables, into the environment; the app only reads process.env](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_env_belongs_to_runner.svg) | [layout.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/layout.md) |
| PROJ-07 | **config/ turns the environment into configuration.** `config/` is the one place of the application's configuration. `config/index.js` reads the environment variables, may load files, and gives the code its configuration ready to use, through one path. | <pre>// config/index.js<br>module.exports = make_config(process.env);<br><br>const config = require('../config');</pre> ![process.env and files go into config/index.js, which gives the code one configuration object, read everywhere through require of config](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_config_from_environment.svg) | [layout.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/layout.md) |
| PROJ-08 | **src/ has a folder per part.** `src/` holds one subdirectory per part of the program. | <pre>src/agent/    src/http/<br>src/android/  src/parser/<br>src/desktop-electron/</pre> ![src/ holding one folder per part: agent, http, android, parser and desktop-electron](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_src_folder_per_part.svg) | [layout.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/layout.md) |
| PROJ-09 | **Shared helpers go to src/helpers/.** Small shared functions go to `src/helpers/`, one function per file. | `src/helpers/array_group.js` ![src/helpers/ with array_group.js, array_index_by.js and string_slug.js, each holding the one function it is named after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_helpers_one_per_file.svg) | [layout.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/layout.md) |
| PROJ-10 | **A unit test sits next to the file it tests.** | <pre>src/helpers/array_group.js<br>src/helpers/array_group.test.js</pre> ![array_group.test.js beside array_group.js in src/helpers/, instead of far away in tests/unit/](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_test_beside_file.svg) | [layout.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/layout.md) |
| PROJ-11 | **tests/ drives the whole program.** `tests/` holds suites that drive the whole program, such as playwright. | ![A playwright suite in tests/ drives a browser, which drives the whole running app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_tests_drive_program.svg) | [layout.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/layout.md) |
| PROJ-12 | **Keep the README short.** `README.md` stays short: what the project is and how to start it. | ![A short README with what the project is and how to start it; a long README of every detail is replaced by it and links to docs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_readme_short.svg) | [layout.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/layout.md) |
| PROJ-13 | **Docs in docs/, notes in notes/, images in img/.** `docs/` holds the official documentation, `notes/` holds working notes — hints and findings made during development — and `img/` holds static images, mostly for the README. | ![docs/ holds the official documentation, notes/ the working notes made during development, img/ the static images, mostly for the README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_docs_notes_img.svg) | [layout.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/layout.md) |
| PROJ-14 | **The project root carries the same standard files.** `.env` is not one of them: it is there only when the runner puts it there (PROJ-06). | <pre>.env.example  .gitignore  Dockerfile  LICENSE<br>README.md  package.json</pre> ![The project root with .env.example, .gitignore, Dockerfile, LICENSE, README.md and package.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_root_standard_files.svg) | [layout.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/layout.md) |
