| PROJ-15 | **A script starts from bin/templ.** A new bash script is a copy of `bin/templ` with what it does not need thrown away. Its header, strict mode included, and the `script` / `scriptdir` / `scriptname` lines always stay; the colors, the exit message, the temporary directory with its `EXIT` trap and the four `echo` lines stay only if the script uses them. | <pre>#!/bin/bash<br><br># http://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#The-Set-Builtin<br># http://redsymbol.net/articles/unofficial-bash-strict-mode<br>set -o nounset -o errexit -o pipefail<br><br>script=&#96;realpath $0&#96;<br>scriptdir=&#96;dirname $script&#96;<br>scriptname=&#96;basename $script&#96;</pre> ![bin/templ: the header and the script, scriptdir and scriptname lines always stay; the colors, the exit message, the temporary directory and the echo lines only if the script needs them](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_script_follows_templ.svg) | [templ](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/bin/templ) |
| PROJ-16 | **bin/configure asks everything up front.** `bin/configure` asks every question it may have — the `sudo` password, a choice, a key — at the very start, before any work. Once the work has started there are no more questions; it never stops halfway, waiting for a password. | ![Questions for a password, a choice and a key come first and the work runs to the end; a run that stops halfway to ask for a password is the wrong way](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_configure_asks_up_front.svg) | [configure.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/configure.md) |
| PROJ-17 | **bin/configure takes sudo once, up front.** `bin/configure` first works out what the run will need, predicting the state after the install. When a step will need `sudo` — an Electron `chrome-sandbox` that is missing, not `root:4755`, or about to be replaced by the install — it takes `sudo -v` up front, and the later calls are `sudo -n`, which fail at once rather than prompt. | <pre>sandbox=node_modules/electron/dist/chrome-sandbox<br>state=&#96;stat -c %U:%a $sandbox 2&gt;/dev/null&#96;<br>wanted=…      # electron in package-lock.json<br>installed=…   # electron in node_modules<br>if &#91; "$wanted" != "$installed" ] \|\| &#91; "$state" != "root:4755" ]; then<br>    sudo -v<br>fi<br><br>sudo -n chown root:root $sandbox   # later: never a prompt</pre> ![bin/configure predicts the state after the install, takes sudo -v once if a step will need it, and later calls sudo -n, which never prompts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_configure_sudo_once.svg) | [configure.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/configure.md) |
| PROJ-18 | **Everything kept lives in data/.** `data/` is the project's permanent data: a restart, a redeploy or a migration does not delete it. Everything the program writes and has to keep lives under `data/`, and nowhere else. Configuration is not there: it comes from `config/` and the environment. | ![Uploads, the database and logs written by the program all live under data/, which survives restarts, redeploys and migrations; configuration comes from config/ and the environment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_data_keeps_everything.svg) | [data.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/data.md) |
| PROJ-19 | **Docker images carry code, not data.** A docker image carries the code, never the data. One mount of `data/` — a named volume or a host directory — is all it takes to keep it; moving the project is moving its `data/` and running it with the same environment. | <pre>docker run -v app-data:/app/data app<br>docker run -v /srv/app/data:/app/data app</pre> ![An image with the code and a data/ volume mounted into the container; docker run -v app-data:/app/data app](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/proj_image_code_not_data.svg) | [data.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/data.md) |

| **REL** | **Packaging and release** — Ship a prebuilt dist/. | | |
| REL-01 | **A project can ship a prebuilt dist/.** A project can distribute a prebuilt `dist/` from the repository, the way Vue, VueRouter, Vuex, jQuery, Bootstrap, Axios, Cuid and Jsondiffpatch do. | `<script src="https://unpkg.com/vue@2.6.11/dist/vue.js"></script>` ![dist/vue.js in the repository, served by unpkg, loaded by a page with a script tag, with no build on the user side](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/rel_ship_prebuilt_dist.svg) | [packaging.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/packaging/packaging.md) |
| REL-02 | **Release order: clean, bump, build, commit, tag.** The release workflow is fixed: ensure there are no changes, increase the version, update `dist/`, commit, tag. `dist/` is updated by the one build, then a copy of `build/` (MP-32). | <pre>test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"<br>npm version $1 --no-git-tag-version<br>rm -rf build<br>npm run build<br>rm -rf dist<br>cp -r build dist<br>git add package.json package-lock.json dist<br>git commit -m "release: v$(...)"<br>git tag v$(...)</pre> ![A release in five steps: no changes, bump the version, build and copy build/ into dist/, commit, tag](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/rel_release_order.svg) | [packaging.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/packaging/packaging.md) |
| REL-03 | **The script commits and tags, not the bump.** Bump the version without committing or tagging, then own both steps in the script. | `npm version $1 --no-git-tag-version` ![npm version without its git tag bumps the version only; the release script then commits and tags](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/rel_script_commits_and_tags.svg) | [packaging.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/packaging/packaging.md) |
| REL-04 | **One command does the whole release.** `bin/release major\|minor\|patch` performs the whole release. | `bin/release patch` ![bin/release patch runs the whole release: clean, bump, build, commit, tag](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/rel_one_command.svg) | [packaging.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/packaging/packaging.md) |
| REL-05 | **A release script runs under bash strict mode.** | `set -o nounset -o errexit -o pipefail` ![set -o nounset stops on an unset variable, errexit on a failing command, pipefail on a failure inside a pipe](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/rel_strict_mode.svg) | [packaging.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/packaging/packaging.md) |
| REL-06 | **A bad argument prints usage to stderr and exits 1.** | <pre>echo usage: release 'major&#124;minor&#124;patch' &gt;&amp;2<br>exit 1</pre> ![bin/release banana prints usage: release major/minor/patch to stderr and exits 1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/rel_bad_argument_usage.svg) | [packaging.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/packaging/packaging.md) |

| GIT-01 | **A commit title is a scope, a colon and a short description.** The scope is one or two words: the part of the project the commit changes, its category. | `maps: placement rules for gates and portals, and map-check` ![The title maps: placement rules for gates and portals, and map-check, as a scope, a colon and a description](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/git_scope_and_description.svg) | [commits.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/commits.md) |
| GIT-02 | **Commit titles are lowercase.** The title is all lowercase, names included. | <pre>readme: elites and arcade saves as the code has them   ✓ yes<br>README: Elites and arcade saves                        ✗ no</pre> ![README: Elites and arcade saves is wrong; readme: elites and arcade saves as the code has them is right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/git_lowercase.svg) | [commits.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/commits.md) |
| GIT-03 | **A commit title is 72 characters at most.** The whole title, scope included, stays within 72 characters. Short is the rule; 72 is the ceiling, not a target. | <pre>maps: one name for the gate jump reach     38<br>docs: build-docs and a github pages workflow     44<br>72 at most</pre> ![Title lengths as bars against a line at 72 characters: 38 and 44 fit, 89 runs past it; the long one is cut to fit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/git_title_72.svg) | [commits.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/commits.md) |
| GIT-04 | **A short body, only when needed.** Details go in a body after one blank line, only when they are really needed. A body is short, in ordinary sentences. | <pre>docs: link the placement rules, gates and portals as they stand<br><br>docs/README.md lists placement.md; objects.md describes gates and<br>portals as the placement rules now put them.</pre> ![A commit with a title, a blank line and a two-line body, beside a commit that needs no body](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/git_short_body.svg) | [commits.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/commits.md) |
| GIT-05 | **A body wraps at 72 characters.** Every line of the body stays within 72 characters, as the title does, and breaks between words. A path, a URL or a command longer than that keeps a line of its own, whole. | <pre>docs: the agents page has a picture for each guide<br><br>Consequences first: the task, its four what-if questions and what each<br>shapes. One example, all cases: only the shown dropdown fixed against<br>every case found.</pre> ![A commit body wrapped at 72 characters, each line ending before a red line at column 72](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/git_body_72.svg) | [commits.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/commits.md) |
| **LOG** | **Logs** — One line, one event, four fields. | | |
| LOG-01 | **One line, one event, four fields.** A log is one stream of lines, as if one infinite file; its files may be split by day (PROJ-05). One physical line records one event, in four fields and nothing else. | `[time][group_uid][sender] details` ![A log line as its four fields, time, group_uid, sender and details, each with what it holds, above three such lines of one log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_one_line_four_fields.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-02 | **Measurements go in details.** Elapsed time, status and every other measurement belong in `details`, not in a field of their own. | `[cd8e5vqp][db_query_end_error] 30.001s ETIMEDOUT` ![The fields of a line with the measurements in details; a fifth bracketed field for 30.001s beside the same line with it in details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_measurements_in_details.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-03 | **`time` is ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds.** | `2026-08-17T16:09:20.185Z` ![An ISO-8601 UTC time split into date, T, time, milliseconds and Z; a local time and an epoch each beside the ISO form](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_time_iso_utc_ms.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-04 | **Omit time when the runtime stamps it.** Include `time` when writing directly to a file; omit it when the runtime already timestamps the line, as docker does. | <pre>&#91;2026-08-17T16:09:20.185Z]&#91;cd8e5vqp]&#91;db_query_begin] name=select_users<br>&#91;cd8e5vqp]&#91;db_query_begin] name=select_users</pre> ![A line written to a file carries its time; under docker, docker's timestamp stands before the app's line, and a doubled time beside the line written once](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_omit_time_when_stamped.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-05 | **Every event carries its group uid.** A group is one unit of work — a request, a job, a cron run. Every event carries its group’s uid, an opaque string, usually a cuid. | ![Four lines of one request, each starting with its group uid cd8e5vqp; a line without a uid beside the same line with it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_group_uid.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-06 | **A group opens with group_spawn.** The first event of a group is `group_spawn`, emitted synchronously before the uid is passed to other work or another event is emitted for the group. A root group omits `parent=`. | <pre>&#91;new_group_uid]&#91;group_spawn] parent=old_group_uid<br>&#91;c1a0root]&#91;group_spawn]</pre> ![A child group and a root group, each opening with group_spawn; a spawn after the first work beside the spawn first](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_group_spawn_first.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-07 | **The caller's uid becomes the parent.** Messages and requests carry the caller’s uid; the receiver uses it as the parent of its new group. | ![A web group sends a job, the message carries its uid, and the worker's group_spawn names it as parent; a spawn without parent beside one with parent=aaa](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_caller_uid_is_parent.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-08 | **A sender names one call site.** `sender` identifies one logging call site, and the name is unique in the whole codebase — a grep for it lands on one place. Think of it as a `const` in a single namespace. | ![A grep for a sender lands on one line of code; one sender in two places beside a name for each place](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_sender_one_call_site.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-09 | **`sender` is snake_case.** | `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$` ![The snake_case pattern of a sender; camelCase and hyphenated senders each beside db_query_begin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_sender_snake_case.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-10 | **Every begin is closed by its end.** A `_begin` event is closed by the same stem with `_end_ok` or `_end_error`, in the same group. An end never appears without its begin in that group. | <pre>&#91;c9k2vf3p]&#91;group_spawn]<br>&#91;c9k2vf3p]&#91;mp4gif_worker_begin]<br>&#91;c9k2vf3p]&#91;mp4gif_worker_end_ok] 4.512s<br><br>&#91;c7t0xb1m]&#91;group_spawn]<br>&#91;c7t0xb1m]&#91;mp4gif_worker_begin]<br>&#91;c7t0xb1m]&#91;mp4gif_worker_end_error] 0.884s ffmpeg exit=1</pre> ![A begin closed by end_ok and a begin closed by end_error; an end with no begin beside the begin and its end](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_begin_closed_by_end.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-11 | **A plain end when the outcome speaks.** Use `_end` when the logged outcome — an HTTP status, say — already says what happened and classifying it as ok or error would mislead. | ![An HTTP request closed by a plain end with its 404; an end_error for the 404 beside the plain end](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_plain_end.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-12 | **Spawn a group only when it pays.** A group costs at least three lines. Spawn one only when the work earns them: seconds of work, or many logging call sites. Do not spawn a group for one short call. | <pre>&#91;bbb]&#91;group_spawn] parent=aaa<br>&#91;bbb]&#91;process_begin]<br>&#91;bbb]&#91;process_end_ok] 0.000s      ✗ noise</pre> ![Three lines of a group spawned for one short call beside the two lines on the caller's group; a group earns its lines with seconds of work or many call sites](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_spawn_only_when_it_pays.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-13 | **Log short work on the caller’s group, not a new one.** When nothing is reported between the two ends, record one event. | <pre>&#91;aaa]&#91;process_begin]<br>&#91;aaa]&#91;process_end_ok] 0.000s<br><br>&#91;aaa]&#91;process_handled] 0.000s     ✓ even better</pre> ![A group spawned for nothing beside the begin and end on the caller's group, and one process_handled line, even better](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_short_work_on_caller.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-14 | **No lone end in a new group.** Two lines are the same noise when a new group holds a lone end. The matching begin was emitted on the parent — keep the pair there. | <pre>&#91;bbb]&#91;group_spawn] parent=aaa<br>&#91;bbb]&#91;process_end_ok] 0.000s      ✗ noise</pre> ![An end that strayed into a new group beside the begin and end together on the parent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_no_lone_end.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-15 | **Details are terse, on one line.** `details` are human-readable and terse, and never contain a physical newline. | ![A details with a newline, its second line without fields, beside the same event on one terse line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_details_one_line.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-16 | **No secrets or payloads in details.** `details` never contain secrets, tokens, signed URLs, URL query values, bodies or headers. Prefer a reference to the payload over the payload. | ![A token, a signed URL and a body each beside a reference that replaces it: a user uid, a file path, a size](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_no_secrets.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-17 | **Simple words bare, the rest JSON-quoted.** A printable ASCII word without spaces, double quotes, backslashes or square brackets is written bare — exactly the bytes that were sent, so it cannot span words, break the line, or mint a fake tag. Every other string is JSON-quoted. | <pre>name=select_users<br>reason="db timeout"<br>value=""</pre> ![A bare word and two JSON-quoted values with why; an unquoted value with a space and a bracketed value each beside its quoted form](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_bare_or_json_quoted.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-18 | **Structures as compact JSON.** Arrays, objects, booleans and null use compact JSON. | `retry=true limits={"soft":10,"hard":25}` ![retry and limits as compact JSON; spaced JSON and a yes for a boolean each beside the compact form](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_structures_compact_json.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-19 | **An unordered list is sorted and prefixed with its count.** Ordered values are not sorted. | <pre>3:&#91;180,783,846]<br>2:&#91;"bar","foo"]<br>0:&#91;]</pre> ![Three lists turned into their sorted, counted form; a list in order of arrival beside 3:(180,783,846)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_unordered_list_sorted.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-20 | **Truncate on UTF-8, count what is cut.** Truncation preserves valid UTF-8 and ends with the number of omitted bytes. | `...+4821` ![A long value cut and 4 821 bytes counted; a cut inside a character beside a whole one ending ...+4821](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_truncate_utf8.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-21 | **Try to keep one log line under 2k UTF-8 bytes.** A log line describes an event; it is not payload storage. | ![A 120-byte event under the 2 KB mark and a 48 000-byte payload far past it; the payload beside a counted, truncated line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_line_under_2k.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-22 | **group_exit is optional; nothing follows it.** `group_exit` is optional and mainly serves to detect leaks. After it is emitted, no producer emits another event for that group; a parent may emit it for work it abandons. Consumers must accept groups without it — its absence makes no claim. | `[group_uid][group_exit]` ![A group closed by group_exit and a note that it is optional; an event after the exit beside the exit last](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_group_exit_optional.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| LOG-23 | **After means emission order, not timestamps.** “After” `group_exit` means producer emission order, not timestamp or collector ingestion order. Buffering may deliver an older event later; that alone is not an error. Without a causal-order signal — preserved per-group order, a shared sequence — cross-process detection is advisory. | ![Two events emitted in one order and received in the other; judging by arrival beside judging by emission](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/log_after_is_emission_order.svg) | [logs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/logs.md) |
| **CSS** | **Classes and styles** — A fixed class order; every class has a rule. | | |
| CSS-01 | **Utilities first, app classes next, local classes last.** Classes inside one `class="…"` attribute keep a fixed order. Plain utilities lead; an app-prefixed class (`vb-*`, `np-*` — one prefix per app, `app-*` in these examples) sorts after all of them, base class included; a file-local `#-*` class is always last. | <pre>layout  spacing  sizing  decoration  typography  app-prefix  local<br><br>&lt;div class="flex-row-c #-root" /&gt;<br>&lt;div class="fluid p30 xpt app-scrollbars-light #-grid" /&gt;<br>&lt;div class="db w80 h80 br4 fit-cover cur-pointer app-background #-preset-img" /&gt;<br>&lt;div class="flex-row-cl gap10 app-font-b14 #-title-trigger" /&gt;</pre> ![The class order as chips, from layout to local, and an example class list labelled by family; local first beside utilities, app, local](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/css_class_order.svg) | [css_classes.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/css_classes.md) |
| CSS-02 | **Item class leads; gap closes the layout.** Within the utilities: an item class (`fluid`, `grow`, `shrink`, `flex-fluid`, `flex-grow`, `flex-nogrow`, `flex-shrink`, `flex-noshrink`, `flex-static`) or a display or position utility (`db`, `abs`) leads where the element carries one; a `gap*` closes the layout group — every `flex*`, `grid*` or split class first, then the gap; `grid*` and `flex*` never share an element; `ph*` precedes `pv*`, and spacing comes before typography. | <pre>fluid flex-row gap10 oa<br>flex-row flex-align-center gap10 mt10<br>flex-col-c gap15<br>grid-foo gap5</pre> ![fluid flex-row gap10 oa and flex-row flex-align-center gap10 mt10 as labelled chips; gap first and flex with grid each beside its right order](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/css_item_class_leads.svg) | [css_classes.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/css_classes.md) |
| CSS-03 | **No class without a rule.** Every class either has a rule in the file’s own style block or is an established project utility. An element that needs no styling stays classless — a label-only class rots and sends the next reader looking for a rule nobody wrote. | <pre>&lt;!-- the wrapper is not styled, so it carries no class --&gt;<br>&lt;div&gt;<br>    &lt;div class="#-funnel-bars"&gt;...&lt;/div&gt;<br>&lt;/div&gt;</pre> ![A wrapper div without a class around a styled #-funnel-bars and its rule; a #-wrapper with no rule beside the classless wrapper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/css_no_class_without_rule.svg) | [css_classes.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/css_classes.md) |
| CSS-04 | **Gap for flex and grid, mg and mi for blocks.** `gap*` spaces the children of a grid or flex container; `mg*` and `mi*` are the block-container forms. The two do not mix. | ![A flex row spaced by gap10 and a block spaced by mg10; mg10 on a flex row beside gap10](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/css_gap_or_mg.svg) | [css_classes.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/css_classes.md) |
| CSS-05 | **Fluid in a split, flex-fluid in a flex.** `fluid` marks the filling child of an `hsplit`/`vsplit` (whose children default to `flex: none`); `flex-fluid` marks the growing child of a plain `flex-row`/`flex-col`. Same CSS — the choice states which container the element sits in. | ![A fluid child filling an hsplit and a flex-fluid child growing in a flex-row; flex-fluid in a split beside fluid](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/css_fluid_or_flex_fluid.svg) | [css_classes.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/css_classes.md) |
| CSS-06 | **Broad before narrow.** An `x*` class usually comes before the setter it clears the way for — the broad class leads and the narrow one corrects it, whichever of the two is the reset. | <pre>&lt;div class="xm ml5" /&gt;   &lt;!-- margin: 0; margin-left: 5px; --&gt;<br>&lt;div class="m5 xml" /&gt;   &lt;!-- margin: 5px; margin-left: 0;  --&gt;</pre> ![xm ml5 and m5 xml with the margins each produces; the reset after the setter beside the reset first](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/css_x_before_setter.svg) | [css_classes.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/css_classes.md) |
| CSS-07 | **Rows and columns are a table.** Rows and columns are a `<table>`, not a stack of flex rows — the columns line up only until one cell is wider. Flex rows stay for content that is genuinely not tabular. | ![A stack of flex rows whose columns drift beside a table whose columns line up, and their code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/css_rows_columns_table.svg) | [css_classes.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/css_classes.md) |
| CSS-08 | **Imports and includes come first.** `@import` comes first in a block; `@include` comes first in a rule, ahead of the property declarations — the mixin brings the base, the block overrides it. | <pre>.#-card<br>    @include app-transition(box-shadow, border-color)<br>    box-sizing: border-box</pre> ![A rule with the include after a declaration beside the same rule with the include first](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/css_imports_includes_first.svg) | [css_classes.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/css_classes.md) |
| CSS-09 | **Transitions come from the mixin.** A `transition:` property is not written by hand — `@include app-transition(props…)` fills it, expanding each property into `<prop> <speed>` at the shared default speed. `app-transition-fast` and `app-transition-debug` are the same mixin at the shared fast and debug speeds. List the exact properties that change, never `all`, and put the include on the base rule rather than the state variant, so the animation covers both directions. The mixin is Sass; plain `.css` files are not checked for it. | `@include app-transition(box-shadow, border-color)` ![The transition mixin expanding into each property at the shared speed; transition: all by hand beside the mixin with exact properties](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/css_transitions_from_mixin.svg) | [css_classes.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/css_classes.md) |
| CSS-10 | **Five families: layout, spacing, sizing, decoration, typography.** What each family holds: layout is the flex/grid/split container and its `flex-*` modifiers; spacing is `p*` / `m*`; sizing is `w*` / `h*` / `max-w*` / `min-h*`; decoration is `br*`, `fit-cover`, `cur-pointer` and the other shape and surface utilities; typography is `fs*` `fw*` `lh*`, then alignment and `nowrap`. | ![The five families, layout, spacing, sizing, decoration and typography, with examples; a mixed-up class list beside the family order](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/css_five_families.svg) | [css_classes.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/css_classes.md) |
| CSS-11 | **A header aligns like its column.** A table header is aligned the way its column's data is: centered data, centered header; right-aligned data, right-aligned header. | ![A table with a centered header over right-aligned numbers beside one whose header aligns as its column](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/css_header_aligns_like_column.svg) | [css_classes.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/css_classes.md) |
| CSS-12 | **One selector per line.** A selector list puts each selector on its own line, the comma closing the line; the brace follows the last one. | <pre>.docs th, .docs td {   ✗ no<br><br>.docs th,<br>.docs td {             ✓ yes</pre> ![Two selectors on one line beside one selector a line, the comma closing each](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/css_one_selector_per_line.svg) | [css_classes.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/css_classes.md) |
| CSS-13 | **One blank line between rules.** Rules stand one blank line apart: each closing brace is followed by one empty line before the next selector — never two, never none. | <pre>.hidden {<br>    display: none !important;<br>}<br>.intro {          ✗ no blank line<br><br>.hidden {<br>    display: none !important;<br>}<br><br>.intro {          ✓ one blank line</pre> ![Two rules with no blank line between them beside the same rules one blank line apart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/css_one_blank_line.svg) | [css_classes.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/css_classes.md) |
| **SQL** | **SQL queries** — MySQL: upper-case keywords; the query laid out like code. | | |
| SQL-01 | **A long query opens and closes on its own line.** A query that spans lines opens its template literal with a line break and closes it on a line of its own; the query is indented one level deeper than the call that runs it. | <pre>await knex.raw(&#96;<br>    UPDATE<br>        user_identities<br>    ...<br>&#96;);</pre> ![A query glued to its knex.raw call beside the query opening and closing on its own lines, indented one level](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/sql_query_opens_own_line.svg) | [sql.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/sql.md) |
| SQL-02 | **Keywords upper case, names lower case.** Every keyword, type and function is upper case; tables, columns, indexes and aliases stay lower case, spelled as the schema spells them. | <pre>SELECT<br>    MIN(id) AS id<br>FROM<br>    user_identities   ✓ yes<br><br>select<br>    min(id) as id<br>from<br>    user_identities   ✗ no</pre> ![A query's tokens as keywords and names; an all-lower-case query beside keywords upper case and names lower case](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/sql_keywords_upper_names_lower.svg) | [sql.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/sql.md) |
| SQL-03 | **Each clause on its own line.** The dialect is MySQL. At the top level of a statement, each clause starts a line of its own — `SELECT`, `FROM`, every `JOIN`, `UPDATE`, `SET`, `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX`, `ON`, `WHERE`, `ALTER TABLE`, `DROP INDEX` — and what the clause takes goes on the next line, indented four spaces. A keyword of several words stays on one line. | <pre>CREATE UNIQUE INDEX<br>    user_identities_primary_user_id_unique<br>ON<br>    user_identities (primary_user_id)<br><br>DROP INDEX<br>    user_identities_primary_user_id_unique<br>ON<br>    user_identities</pre> ![A CREATE UNIQUE INDEX whose clauses run on beside each clause on its line with its operand indented under it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/sql_each_clause_own_line.svg) | [sql.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/sql.md) |
| SQL-04 | **A subquery body is indented between its parentheses.** A subquery opens with `(` at the end of the line that uses it; its body is indented one level, and `)` closes it on a line of its own at that line's indent, followed by the alias. | <pre>WHERE id IN (<br>    SELECT id FROM (<br>        SELECT MIN(id) AS id<br>        ...<br>    ) AS oldest<br>)</pre> ![A flat nested subquery beside the same subquery indented a level per pair of parentheses](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/sql_subquery_indented.svg) | [sql.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/sql.md) |
| SQL-05 | **Short expressions may stay on one line.** A short expression can stay on one line: a `WHERE` that opens a subquery, even at the top level, and the clauses inside a subquery. | <pre>WHERE id IN (<br>    SELECT id FROM (<br>        SELECT MIN(id) AS id<br>        FROM user_identities</pre> ![A WHERE split to the word beside short expressions kept on one line inside the subquery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/sql_short_expressions_one_line.svg) | [sql.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/sql.md) |
| SQL-06 | **One ALTER TABLE action per clause.** Each action of an `ALTER TABLE` is a clause of its own, its operand indented under it; the comma between two actions ends the first operand's line. A column definition stays whole on its line. | <pre>ALTER TABLE<br>    user_identities<br>DROP INDEX<br>    user_identities_primary_user_id_unique,<br>DROP COLUMN<br>    primary_user_id</pre> ![An ALTER TABLE with its actions run together beside one action per clause, each operand indented](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/sql_alter_table_one_action.svg) | [sql.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/sql.md) |
| **VUE** | **Vue 2** — Components that behave like the platform. | | |
| VUE-01 | **Every component is provided with three global methods through a mixin.** | <pre>px(value)        // format a pixel value<br>uid(&#91;name])      // ids unique across components<br>emit_input(value) // return a value from an input</pre> ![One globals mixin hands px, uid and emit_input to every component](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_global_methods_mixin.svg) | [vue-globals.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-globals.md) |
| VUE-02 | **Ids come from uid.** Generated ids are bound to the current element and are what `id` and `label[for]` use. The name `uid` was chosen so it does not conflict with the `id` attribute every element may carry. | <pre>uid: function (name) {<br>    return name ? &#96;c${this.&#95;uid}&#95;${name}&#96; : &#96;c${this.&#95;uid}&#96;;<br>},</pre> ![The component's _uid 42 and uid('email') make the id c42_email, used by both the label and the input](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_ids_from_uid.svg) | [vue-globals.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-globals.md) |
| VUE-03 | **Spell out `v-on` and `v-bind`.** The shorthands `@` and `:` are not used. | `<img v-bind:src="photo.thumbnail_url" v-bind:alt="photo.title" />` ![The shorthands :src and @click beside the same element written with v-bind:src and v-on:click](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_spell_out_v_on_v_bind.svg) | [vue-formatting.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-formatting.md) |
| VUE-04 | **Attributes keep one order.** | `ref v-if v-for v-on v-bind:ref v-bind [...] class type placeholder title` ![The ten attributes in their order, ref first and title last, and an input element written in that order](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_attribute_order.svg) | [vue-formatting.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-formatting.md) |
| VUE-05 | **Lift v-if off a v-for.** Avoid `v-if` and `v-for` on the same component — lift the condition to a `<template>`. | <pre>&lt;template v-if="items"&gt;<br>    &lt;div v-for="item in items" v-bind:key="item.uid"&gt;<br>        {{ item.title }}<br>    &lt;/div&gt;<br>&lt;/template&gt;</pre> ![A div carrying both v-for and v-if beside the condition lifted to a template around the loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_lift_v_if_off_v_for.svg) | [vue-formatting.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-formatting.md) |
| VUE-06 | **Compound directive values in parentheses.** A simple directive value stays bare; a compound one is wrapped in parentheses. Every directive — `v-if`, `v-else-if`, `v-show`, `v-on`, `v-bind`. Simple is a single identifier, member access, method call, template literal or unary negation; compound is anything carrying a binary operator or a ternary. Only in a template: inside an attribute's quotes a compound value is easy to miss, and the parentheses show it. The same value moved into script, a computed or a method, loses them and follows FMT-27. | <pre>&lt;template v-if="is_ready"&gt;<br>&lt;template v-if="(is_loading_fonts &#124;&#124; is_loading_images)"&gt;<br>&lt;div v-bind:class="(compact ? 'narrow' : 'wide')" /&gt;</pre> ![An operator and a ternary left bare beside the same values in parentheses, and a simple value wrapped beside it bare](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_compound_in_parentheses.svg) | [vue-formatting.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-formatting.md) |
| VUE-07 | **An input works like a native input.** Anything which takes data from a user is called an **input** and must work as a normal INPUT element. | 1. takes data from the `value` property<br>2. emits an **input** event<br>3. respects the **disabled** state<br>4. respects the `readonly` attribute<br>5. reacts to clicks on the associated LABEL<br>6. reacts to mouse hover from that LABEL<br>7. injects and uses `app_form_input_id`<br>8. takes focus with the TAB key ![app-input-email takes value, disabled and readonly, emits input, and answers a click on its label and the Tab key like an input](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_input_like_native.svg) | [vue-input.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-input.md) |
| VUE-08 | **Avoid generic inputs.** Avoid generic inputs — those with a lot of properties like `min`, `max`, `step`. | ![One app-input-number with min, max, step and more beside app-input-percent, app-input-px and app-input-year](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_avoid_generic_inputs.svg) | [vue-input.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-input.md) |
| VUE-09 | **Forms submit by button and Enter.** Compose forms from `app-form-div` and `app-label`, inside a `<form>` whose `submit` the submit button and the Enter key both reach. | <pre>&lt;form v-on:submit.prevent="submit" class="mg10"&gt;<br>    &lt;app-form-div class="flex-row gap10"&gt;<br>        &lt;app-label&gt;Email:&lt;/app-label&gt;<br>        &lt;app-input-email v-model="user.email" /&gt;<br>    &lt;/app-form-div&gt;<br>&lt;/form&gt;</pre> ![A form whose field (Enter) and Submit button both reach its one submit handler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_form_submit_button_and_enter.svg) | [vue-form.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-form.md) |
| VUE-10 | **Cancel and submit close the form.** A form’s buttons close the form: cancel returns `false` through vue-modal’s `modal.return`, submit is a `type="submit"` button. | <pre>&lt;app-button-orange v-on:click="modal.return(false)"&gt;<br>    Cancel<br>&lt;/app-button-orange&gt;<br>&lt;app-button-green type="submit"&gt;<br>    Submit<br>&lt;/app-button-green&gt;</pre> ![A Rename file form: Cancel returns false through modal.return and closes; Submit is a type submit button that saves and closes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_cancel_submit_close.svg) | [vue-form.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-form.md) |
| VUE-11 | **One button, one class.** | ![A button assembled from btn btn-green btn-lg beside one class, button-green](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_one_button_one_class.svg) | [vue-button.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-button.md) |
| VUE-12 | **A slider thumb moves from 0 to 100%.** A slider is usually a container and a thumb. Prefer positioning the thumb with `top` or `left` from `0` to `100%` — `0` means empty, `100%` means full. | <pre>left: 0      // empty<br>left: 100%   // full</pre> ![Three sliders with the thumb at left 0, 50% and 100%: empty, half and full](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_slider_thumb_percent.svg) | [vue-slider.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-slider.md) |
| VUE-13 | **One SVG icon per file.** Each SVG icon goes into its own `svg-icon-*.vue` file, containing only a TEMPLATE element with an SVG inside. | <pre>&lt;template&gt;<br>    &lt;svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" xmlns="http&#58;//www&#46;w3.org/2000/svg"&gt;<br>        &lt;path fill="currentColor" d="..." /&gt;<br>    &lt;/svg&gt;<br>&lt;/template&gt;</pre> ![A folder of svg-icon-*.vue files and the one file content: a template with an SVG whose path fills currentColor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_one_icon_per_file.svg) | [vue-svg-icon.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-svg-icon.md) |
| VUE-14 | **Icons use currentColor.** SVG icons respect the `currentColor` CSS property. | `<path fill="currentColor" d="..." />` ![The same archive icon in a plain, an accent and a danger button, taking each button text colour](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_icons_current_color.svg) | [vue-svg-icon.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-svg-icon.md) |
| VUE-15 | **Component options keep one order.** | `props inject provide mixins data computed watch methods mounted created beforeDestroy` ![The eleven component options in their order, from props to beforeDestroy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_component_options_order.svg) | [vue-components.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-components.md) |
| VUE-16 | **Name a handler by event and button text.** An event handler is named after the UI part it is bound to — the event, then the button text. | <pre>&lt;button v-on:click="click_approve"&gt;<br>    Approve<br>&lt;/button&gt;</pre> ![The Approve button handled by click_approve; handle_click beside it, saying nothing of the button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_handler_by_event_and_text.svg) | [vue-components.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-components.md) |
| VUE-17 | **A handler on an icon is named after the icon.** | <pre>&lt;button v-on:click="click_icon_archive"&gt;<br>    &lt;svg-icon-archive /&gt;<br>&lt;/button&gt;</pre> ![An archive icon button handled by click_icon_archive; click_button beside it, naming no button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_handler_on_icon.svg) | [vue-components.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-components.md) |
| VUE-18 | **Rename the handler with its label.** After the text or icon is changed, rename the corresponding event handler. | `Approve → Accept     // click_approve → click_accept` ![Approve with click_approve; after the label becomes Accept, click_approve left stale beside click_accept](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_rename_handler_with_label.svg) | [vue-components.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-components.md) |
| VUE-19 | **Empty elements close themselves.** An element without a body closes itself — a component, an HTML element and a void element alike. This holds in `.vue` files and string templates; an in-DOM template is parsed by the browser first. | <pre>&lt;th&gt;&lt;/th&gt;   ✗ no<br>&lt;th /&gt;       ✓ yes<br><br>&lt;app-input-email v-model="user.email" /&gt;</pre> ![An empty th, an empty component and a bare br left open, each beside its self-closing form](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_empty_elements_self_close.svg) | [vue-formatting.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-formatting.md) |
| VUE-20 | **A piece shown in two places is a component.** Whatever the screen shows in more than one place, a badge most often, is a Vue component of its own, used in each place. Never the same markup and classes copied: a change then reaches some copies and misses the others. | <pre>&lt;span class="flex-row-cl gap5 br999 #-reply"&gt;   ✗ no<br>    In progress {{ detail }}<br>&lt;/span&gt;<br><br>&lt;badge-in-progress v-bind:detail="detail" /&gt;   ✓ yes</pre> ![One badge-in-progress component used in the list and in the detail, beside markup copied into each place](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_piece_in_two_places_is_component.svg) | [vue-components.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-components.md) |
| VUE-21 | **Named kind first.** A component is named `<kind>-<what it says>`, as icons are `svg-icon-*`. Sorted by name, every component of a kind sits together. | <pre>badge-filing<br>badge-in-progress<br>badge-no-reply</pre> ![Components named what-kind scatter when sorted; named kind-what, each kind sorts together](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_named_kind_first.svg) | [vue-components.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-components.md) |
| VUE-22 | **What changes is a prop.** What differs from place to place goes in as a prop: a count, a time, a plan's progress. The component holds the rest. | <pre>&lt;badge-new v-bind:count="3" /&gt;              // 3 new<br>&lt;badge-in-progress detail="for 4 h" /&gt;</pre> ![badge-new with count 3 and 12 and badge-in-progress with a detail, each rendering its own badge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_what_changes_is_prop.svg) | [vue-components.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-components.md) |
| VUE-23 | **A variant is a suffix.** A smaller or otherwise different form is a component of its own, named with a suffix; never a second copy written by hand where it is needed. | `badge-in-progress → badge-in-progress-sm` ![badge-in-progress and its smaller badge-in-progress-sm; a badge shrunk by a class at one place beside the variant](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_variant_is_suffix.svg) | [vue-components.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-components.md) |
| VUE-24 | **A kind shares one look through one mixin.** What every component of a kind shares, its shape, size and type, comes from one Sass mixin; each component sets only its own colours. | <pre>.#-root<br>    @include app-badge<br>    background: var(--accent-soft)<br>    color: var(--accent)</pre> ![The app-badge mixin gives shape, size and type to badge-new, badge-done and badge-waiting, each with its own colours](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/vue_kind_shares_mixin.svg) | [vue-components.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/vue2/vue-components.md) |
| **UI** | **UI appearance** — How a screen looks. | | |
| UI-01 | **Every screen has a light/dark switch.** An app screen, a report, a standalone page: each shows a switch the reader can click. Following the OS setting alone does not count. One exception: a page made only to be photographed for a rule's picture keeps no switch. | ![An app screen, a report and a standalone page, each with a theme switch; following the OS setting alone beside a switch on every screen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/ui_every_screen_has_switch.svg) | [theme_switch.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/theme_switch.md) |
| UI-02 | **Two states, one shared icon button.** Show the current theme: sun for Light, crescent for Dark. Use `img/theme-sun.svg` and `img/theme-moon.svg`; size and border may vary. Click toggles directly, with no menu, System or Auto option. | <pre>Sun: Light → Crescent: Dark → Sun: Light</pre> ![One button cycling sun, crescent, sun with each click; a Light, Dark, System menu beside it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/ui_two_states_one_button.svg) | [theme_switch.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/theme_switch.md) |
| UI-03 | **The dark theme redefines the light colors.** The light colors live on `:root`; the dark theme sets the same variables under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`. | <pre>:root {<br>    --color-bg: #FFFFFF;<br>    --color-text: #1B1F23;<br>}<br>:root&#91;data-theme="dark"] {<br>    --color-bg: #15181C;<br>    --color-text: #E6E8EB;<br>}</pre> ![:root sets --color-bg and --color-text; :root(data-theme="dark") sets the same names to other values](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/ui_dark_redefines_light.svg) | [theme_switch.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/theme_switch.md) |
| UI-04 | **The theme is set before the page shows.** The page reads the saved choice from `localStorage` (the OS setting once, when nothing is saved), puts it on `<html>` as `data-theme`, and saves each new choice; storage access sits in `try`/`catch`. | `document.documentElement.dataset.theme = theme;` ![The page reads localStorage and sets data-theme on html before the first paint; painting light then switching flashes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/ui_theme_set_before_show.svg) | [theme_switch.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/theme_switch.md) |
| UI-05 | **The switch stays in reach on a long page.** When the header scrolls away, a copy of the switch appears at the right end of the sticky bar. | ![At the top the switch is in the header; scrolled, a copy rides at the right end of the sticky bar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/ui_switch_stays_in_reach.svg) | [theme_switch.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/theme_switch.md) |
| UI-06 | **Every project page opens with the same header.** The project on the left; GitHub and the theme switch on the right; search and section links between them, the search lined up with the content column. | ![the parts of a page header, left to right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/drafts/page-header-structure.png) | [page_header.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/page_header.md) |
| UI-07 | **Left: icon, name, version.** The project's icon when it has one, its name, and its released version. | <pre>&#91;icon]  Authwall Docs  v1.16.0</pre> ![A header with the icon, the name Authwall Docs and the released version v1.16.0; an unreleased version beside it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/ui_header_left_icon_name_version.svg) | [page_header.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/page_header.md) |
| UI-08 | **Right: the links, then the theme switch, always last.** The GitHub icon links to the repository; other links, such as Twitter or Facebook, sit beside it. However many links a project has, the switch stays at the right edge, the same on every page. The icons look alike: one size, no frame on any of them. | <pre>&#91;GitHub]  &#91;Twitter]  &#91;Current theme icon]</pre> ![Headers with two links and with one, the theme switch last at the right edge in both](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/ui_header_right_links_then_switch.svg) | [page_header.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/page_header.md) |
| UI-21 | **A table keeps its columns while they fit.** With room on the screen every column stays on top, and the table is read at a glance, without a click. Only a table that turns into a grid — cells wrapping over several lines, words or paths broken mid-word, columns cut off — folds columns into its rows' details, and only as many as it must, at that width: the same table keeps more columns on a wide screen than on a phone. | ![on a wide screen a table folded down to name and state beside the same table with every column on top; at phone width a table broken mid-word into a grid beside the same rows with name and state, one opened to show what folded](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/drafts/table-details.png) | [table_details.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/table_details.md) |
| UI-22 | **What a row is and its state never fold.** The columns that tell what a row is and what state it is in always stay on top. The others fold one at a time, the least needed first, until the rest fit on one line; a column the reader compares across rows folds last. | <pre>wide:    logs  ~/logs.sock  vps1  ● ready<br>phone:   ▸ logs  ● ready</pre> | [table_details.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/table_details.md) |
| UI-23 | **A click opens what folded, below the row.** A click on the row opens the folded columns right under it, as wide as the table: one line each, its label and its value; a long value wraps there whole. Only what folded is there, never a repeat of what the row shows; a table with nothing folded has no click and no chevron. Another click closes them; the row clicked stays where it was (UIM-01). | <pre>▾ charts-on-the-other-side  ● ready<br>    Listens on    laptop · ~/charts.sock<br>    Carried to    vps1 · 127.0.0.1:41941<br>    Last failure  ECONNRESET, 10:42</pre> | [table_details.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/table_details.md) |
| **UIM** | **UI mechanics** — How a screen works. | | |
| UIM-01 | **Nothing jumps.** In a list or a grid, the item the reader works with, the one selected or being looked at, stays where it is on the screen while the app adds, removes or grows items above, below or beside it — a new message, a summary that finishes loading; the scroll position adjusts instead, as far as the list's ends allow. A control that docks or hides as the page scrolls is outside this rule. | ![a summary grows above; on the left the message being read drops, on the right it stays](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/drafts/scroll-anchoring.gif) [▶ Try it](https://vbarbarosh.github.io/rules/drafts/scroll-anchoring.html) | [scroll_anchoring.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/scroll_anchoring.md) |
| UIM-02 | **Keep the place yourself; the browser won't.** Before such a change, note the element in the middle of the view and where it is on the screen; after the change, scroll by however far it moved. The browser keeps the place only when the change is entirely above the view: not at the very top, not when the growing block is itself on screen, not after a re-render. | <pre>const keep = scroll_keep(scroller);<br>await keep(async function () {<br>    summary.text = text;<br>    await vm.$nextTick();<br>});</pre> ![A block above grows: alone the browser lets the line being read move 120 px; scroll_keep holds it at 0 px](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/uim_keep_the_place.svg) [▶ Try it](https://vbarbarosh.github.io/rules/drafts/scroll-anchoring.html) | [scroll_anchoring.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/scroll_anchoring.md) |
| UIM-03 | **Test it.** For each kind of change, a test notes where the middle element is, makes the change, and checks it moved 0 px — at the top of the view and in the middle. One more check runs without the fix and must see the jump. | `assert.equal(shift, 0);` ![The test notes the middle element, makes the change, measures and asserts 0 px; without the fix it must see the jump](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/uim_test_it.svg) | [scroll_anchoring.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/scroll_anchoring.md) |
| UIM-04 | **A file input also takes a drop.** Anything that lets the user pick files also takes files dragged onto it; anything that lets them pick a whole folder also takes a folder dragged onto it. | ![a file field and a folder field: each picked with its button, or dragged onto it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/drafts/file-drop.png) | [file_drop.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/file_drop.md) |
| UIM-05 | **The drop takes what the dialog takes.** The same file types, one or many; a whole folder when the dialog picks folders, read file by file. A dropped file goes down the same path as a picked one. | <pre>file_drop_bind(element, input, take);<br><br>// the input says what the dialog takes<br>for (const entry of entries) {<br>    if (entry.isFile \|\| input.webkitdirectory) {<br>        await entry_files_read(entry, files);<br>    }<br>}<br>take(files_as_dialog_takes(files.length ? files : &#91;...event.dataTransfer.files], input));</pre> ![A picked and a dropped file both go through files_as_dialog_takes to take(files)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/uim_drop_takes_what_dialog_takes.svg) | [file_drop.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/file_drop.md) |
| UIM-06 | **Show the drop target; never lose the page.** The element lights up while files are dragged over it, and a file dropped beside it does not open in the tab. | <pre>window.addEventListener('dragover', v =&gt; v.preventDefault());<br>window.addEventListener('drop', v =&gt; v.preventDefault());</pre> ![A drop zone lit while dragging and a file dropped beside it ignored, beside a tab that opens the file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/uim_show_drop_target.svg) | [file_drop.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/file_drop.md) |
| UIM-07 | **Trust the user: no "Are you sure?".** Delete, rename, move, cancel: it happens at once, and the user keeps working. | ![not a dialog on every delete, but done at once with Undo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/drafts/no-confirmations.png) | [no_confirmations.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/no_confirmations.md) |
| UIM-08 | **Undo instead.** A deleted thing goes to a trash; a rename, an edit or a move can be undone. The way back is right there after the action. | `Deleted · Undo` ![A delete confirmation and a rename with no way back, beside Deleted · Undo and Renamed · Undo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/uim_undo_instead.svg) | [no_confirmations.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/no_confirmations.md) |
| UIM-09 | **Confirm only what cannot be undone and costs a lot.** Closing an account, erasing data for good. Even then, not an OK/Cancel box but a deliberate step: typing the name, or a link sent by email. | ![An OK/Cancel box for closing an account beside typing the account name to close it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/uim_confirm_only_costly.svg) | [no_confirmations.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/no_confirmations.md) |
| UIM-10 | **Use optimistic updates; the user keeps working.** Keep the backend snapshot immutable and local pending changes separate. Show the local change and send its update immediately. After acknowledgement, reread the backend, replace the snapshot, and clear only the pending change confirmed by that result; preserve later actions and reject stale refreshes. Show the change where the user made it, at once, marked as waiting, whatever route it takes inside. Keep failures visible as unsynchronized and retry safely; if only the reread failed, retry that step. | <pre>Read → local overlay → update → acknowledgement<br>→ refresh → replace snapshot → clear confirmed overlay</pre> ![Send is pressed: on the left the comment is nowhere for 2 seconds, then it shows; on the right it shows at once marked Sending, and the mark goes when the server has it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/drafts/optimistic-updates.gif) | [optimistic_updates.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/optimistic_updates.md) |
| UIM-11 | **Typing focuses the main search, first character included.** On a page with one primary search/filter, typing outside editable fields focuses it immediately and enters the first character too. Local inputs retain their typing; respect shortcuts and native keyboard behavior. | <pre>Click background → type sm → main filter contains sm</pre> ![Typing s then m outside a field puts sm in the main filter; a local field keeps its own typing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/uim_typing_focuses_search.svg) | [main_search.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/main_search.md) |
| UIM-12 | **Select the first actionable item by default.** In a list of action targets, the first visible actionable item in displayed order is selected by default; Enter acts on it. An explicit user selection wins. A new filtered list defaults to its first actionable item; an empty list has no action. | <pre>SQLite, LinkedIn → Enter opens SQLite</pre> ![SQLite, first in the list, is selected, so Enter opens it; nothing selected beside it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/uim_first_actionable_selected.svg) | [default_list_item.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/default_list_item.md) |
| UIM-13 | **Show only what works.** A control the app already knows will fail is not drawn as if it would work: an expired option, the button of an ended chat, an action the user has no right to. Nobody presses a button to be told "Sorry, this has expired". | ![a support chat: on the left End chat answers Sorry, this option has timed out; on the right the expired options are gone and the reason is shown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/drafts/dead-controls.png) | [dead_controls.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/dead_controls.md) |
| UIM-14 | **Ask the action first: a dry run.** Every action can answer "would it work now?" without doing anything. The screen asks before drawing the control, and again whenever the answer can change; a button that expires on screen changes at that moment, not on the next click. | <pre>can_end_chat(chat) → false<br>→ no End chat button</pre> ![can_end_chat(chat) is asked before drawing: true shows End chat, false draws none; a button that says Sorry after the click beside it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/uim_dry_run.svg) | [dead_controls.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/dead_controls.md) |
| UIM-15 | **No means hidden, or disabled with the reason on it.** Hide what nobody would look for there; disable what the user expects in its place, with the reason written on it or beside it. Never a control whose only answer comes after the click. | `Expired yesterday at 10:51` ![A control hidden where nobody looks for it, or disabled with Expired yesterday at 10:51 beside it; a Sorry after the click beside that](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/uim_hidden_or_disabled_with_reason.svg) | [dead_controls.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/dead_controls.md) |
| **DOC** | **Writing the rules** — How a document in this repo is built. | | |
| DOC-01 | **A document has two halves.** The author writes the top half, compressed around what he already knows; the AI writes the bottom half, restating it for a reader who lacks that context. | ![A document as two stacked halves: the author's compressed notes on top, the AI's restated explanation below, each written by one of them](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/doc_two_halves.svg) | [WRITING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/WRITING.md) |
| DOC-02 | **Author sources govern the explanation.** Read the top half and applicable manually approved rules. An approved entry may explicitly clarify older wording within its scope; if the sources disagree without such a decision, ask before regenerating. | ![The author's half and the approved rules feed the AI, which writes the explanation; when they disagree with no approved entry, the AI asks first](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/doc_author_sources_govern.svg) | [WRITING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/WRITING.md) |
| DOC-03 | **No AI patches the top half.** The one exception is an explicit request from the author. | ![An AI rewording of the author's line, wrong, beside the line kept word for word; the one exception is the author asking for it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/doc_no_ai_patches_top.svg) | [WRITING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/WRITING.md) |
| DOC-04 | **Regenerate the bottom half from both sources, never edit it.** After the top half or an applicable manually approved rule changes, regenerate the explanation from both. Preserve approved decisions and their scope. | ![A change on top leads to the whole bottom half written again from both sources; patching one line of the bottom is wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/doc_regenerate_bottom.svg) | [WRITING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/WRITING.md) |
| DOC-05 | **Usually a heading starts the bottom half.** Most of the time the bottom half starts with a `#` heading, and that heading is the boundary. A `---` line or a closing fence before it is decoration. There is no strict marker. | `--- ✨ AI-Generated Content Below ✨ ---` ![The author's notes, a decorative --- line, then the # heading that is the real boundary of the AI's half](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/doc_heading_starts_bottom.svg) | [WRITING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/WRITING.md) |
| DOC-06 | **One audit, one file; its register is the issue list.** The report of a full audit is one file, `notes/audit-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`. The projects have no issue tracker: the finding register of the newest audit note is the issue list, and later audits refer to findings by their ids. | `notes/audit-2026-09-02.md` ![The notes/ folder of audit files, the newest one's finding register serving as the issue list of ids](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/doc_one_audit_one_file.svg) | [audit_note.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/audit_note.md) |
| DOC-07 | **Audit notes keep one section order.** An audit note keeps one order: title, repository line, scope, verdict with a health-at-a-glance table, finding register, findings, what is good, recommended order of work, status of prior findings, file inventory. | ![The ten sections of an audit note in their fixed order, from the title to the file inventory](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/doc_audit_section_order.svg) | [audit_note.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/audit_note.md) |
| DOC-08 | **Scope says what ran and what did not.** The scope lists every check actually run, and what was not exercised. A check which was not run is said so; it is never implied. | ![The checks that ran listed beside the one that did not, with the reason it was not run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/doc_scope_ran_and_not.svg) | [audit_note.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/audit_note.md) |
| DOC-09 | **Findings have permanent ids and evidence.** A finding id is `<PROJECT>-NN`, never reused and never renumbered. Each finding is one section citing `file:line` and the evidence — the quoted lines, the command which was run and what it printed. A finding in the author's own text is reported only; it is not patched. | `### DEMO-01 Classes banned in one file, shown in another (high)` ![A finding with its id, file and line, quoted code and the command with its output; reusing an old id is wrong, the next one is new](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/doc_findings_ids_evidence.svg) | [audit_note.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/audit_note.md) |
| DOC-10 | **Audit notes have no top half and stay untracked.** An audit note is written by the AI as a whole, so it has no top half and no separator. It is left untracked; it is committed only on request. | ![An audit note written whole by the AI, shown untracked by git status, committed only on request](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/doc_audit_note_untracked.svg) | [audit_note.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/audit_note.md) |
| DOC-11 | **Keep manually approved rules outside regenerated text.** Record only explicit author decisions in MANUALLY_APPROVED_RULES.md, with scope, approval date and evidence. Read applicable entries when rewriting explanations. Maintain the approval file; never regenerate it or treat an AI suggestion as approval. | <pre>author source + manually approved rules<br>→ regenerated explanation</pre> ![The author's source and the approved rules feed the explanation; an AI suggestion filed as an approval is wrong, an entry with the author's message is right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/doc_approved_rules_apart.svg) | [MANUALLY_APPROVED_RULES.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/MANUALLY_APPROVED_RULES.md) |
| DOC-12 | **A document without an author section is open to requested edits.** A document with no author notes above a heading is an ordinary file: the AI edits it for the task asked. Where the author's section exists, it stays on top and is never overwritten. When its end is unclear, ask first. | <pre>author notes        → never overwritten<br># Heading<br>explanation         → regenerated<br><br>no author notes     → edited on request</pre> ![A file with author notes, kept on top while the explanation below is regenerated, beside a file without them, edited on request](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/doc_without_author_section.svg) | [WRITING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/WRITING.md) |
| DOC-13 | **A glossary keeps the author's terms; the AI explains below them.** Everything before the first `## ` section (title, note, groups, term list) is the author's and is never rewritten. Each `## ` section explains one term and is regenerated from the author's line. | <pre># Testing (TEST)           yours<br>- Flaky Test – …           yours<br><br>## Intermittent failures   AI</pre> ![A glossary file: the author's title and term list on top, never rewritten, and below one AI section per term](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/doc_glossary_terms_and_sections.svg) | [WRITING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/WRITING.md) |
| DOC-14 | **A GIF shows its time and its progress.** Every GIF in the docs is recorded at 30 frames a second, counts its time from 0 at its first frame in a corner, and has a thin bar along its top that fills as it plays; both start again when it loops. | ![A GIF frame with nothing to tell how far in it is, beside one with a bar two thirds along its top and 3.07 s in its corner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/doc_gif_time_and_progress.svg) | [gifs.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/drafts/gifs.md) |
| **LINT** | **Stated by the linter** — Rules that only LINTING.md and the preset spell out. | | |
| LINT-01 | **Spaces around operators, except `*`, `/` and `**`.** `*`, `/` and `**` are tight. Every other binary, logical and assignment operator has a space on each side. | <pre>const x = a&#42;b + c/d - e&#42;&#42;2;<br>const y = a % 2;</pre> ![Spaced multiplication and tight addition, wrong, beside tight * / ** and spaced + - %, right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/lint_operator_spacing.svg) | [LINTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/LINTING.md) |
| LINT-02 | **Space before an anonymous function's parenthesis.** An anonymous function has a space before its parenthesis; a named one has none. | <pre>server.on('error', function (error) {<br>});<br><br>function main()<br>{<br>}</pre> ![function(error) without a space and function main () with one, wrong, beside function (error) and function main(), right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/lint_anonymous_function_space.svg) | [LINTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/LINTING.md) |
| LINT-03 | **Tiny arrows fit one line.** A tiny arrow is a single-line expression callback or value factory, passed as a call argument or as an object property value; an empty `() => {}` is one too (FMT-32). Options-style methods retain function expressions (FMT-12); literal `methods: {...}` tables reject arrows. It fits one line; the number of parameters does not matter. A lone value/event parameter is `v`, `vv` only when `v` is already taken where it stands (VAR-09); an error parameter stays `e` at every depth (VAR-05), including `.catch`, `.then` rejection callbacks and EventEmitter error listeners. It is taken whole — `v => v.uid`, not `({uid}) => uid` — and a last parameter it does not use is not declared: `() => run()`, not `v => run()`. A named helper is a function declaration. | ![Four wrong arrows beside their right forms: a destructured parameter, err for an error, a named helper as an arrow, an arrow in methods](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/lint_tiny_arrows.svg) | [LINTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/LINTING.md) |
| LINT-04 | **Use for...of, not forEach.** `forEach` does not exist. Use `for...of`. | <pre>items.forEach(function (item) {   ✗ no<br>});<br><br>for (const item of items) {       ✓ yes<br>}</pre> ![items.forEach(...), wrong, beside for (const item of items), right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/lint_for_of.svg) | [LINTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/LINTING.md) |
| LINT-06 | **Imports first: side effects, defaults, named.** Imports are the first statements of a file, one statement per line, in up to three blocks: side-effect imports — `import './x'`, a bare `require('x')` — first, in the order they run; then the sorted default imports; then, if set apart, the sorted named imports (`{foo, bar}`). One blank line may separate the blocks. | ![The three import blocks in order: side effects as they run, sorted defaults, sorted named imports](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/lint_imports_first.svg) | [LINTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/LINTING.md) |
| LINT-07 | **The project picks its module format.** Module format is the consuming project’s choice: JavaScript defaults to ES modules, `.cjs` is CommonJS, and the sorting rule supports both import forms. CommonJS-only is this repository’s own rule. | ![ES modules for .js, CommonJS for .cjs, and CommonJS only in this repository](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/lint_module_format.svg) | [LINTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/LINTING.md) |
| LINT-08 | **A layout and its gap share a class value.** `gap*` closes the layout group: the flex/grid/split container, then its `flex-*` modifiers, then the gap. Put a layout and its gap in the same class value. | ![A layout and its gap in separate class values, wrong, beside them in one value, right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/lint_layout_gap_together.svg) | [LINTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/LINTING.md) |
| LINT-09 | **Font size and weight before line height.** Within typography, `fs*` and `fw*` come before `lh*`. Several local `#-*` classes together form the final group. | ![Line height before font size and a local class before a utility, wrong, beside fs, fw, lh and local classes last, right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/lint_font_before_line_height.svg) | [LINTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/LINTING.md) |
| LINT-10 | **Write #- only where the loader replaces it.** `#-` is written only in the forms the hashtag loader replaces: a double-quoted `class`, `card_class` or attribute ending in `-class` / `:class`; `.#-` in a style block; and the exact single-quoted `'.#-` form in JavaScript. | ![Four #- forms the loader skips beside the forms it replaces: double-quoted class attributes, '.#- in JavaScript, .#- in a style block](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/lint_hashtag_forms.svg) | [LINTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/LINTING.md) |
| LINT-11 | **Every #- class has a real style.** Each statically known `#-*` class has a nonempty style selector in the same component. Declarations, includes and extends count as styles; an empty rule, a variable-only rule, or a mention inside `:not(...)` does not. | ![An empty #- rule and a #- class only inside :not(), wrong, beside rules with declarations, right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/lint_hashtag_has_style.svg) | [LINTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/LINTING.md) |
| LINT-12 | **A Vue script indents four spaces.** A Vue `<script>` is indented four spaces with one base indent. | ![A Vue script with no base indent and two spaces, wrong, beside one base indent and four spaces, right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vbarbarosh/rules/main/img/rules/lint_vue_script_indent.svg) | [LINTING.md](https://github.com/vbarbarosh/rules/blob/main/LINTING.md) |
